English: Forward to the Encyclopedia: Herein is contained the sum of the knowledge of our civilisation, gathered in one place, of all the wondrous and strange peoples of the world. Below is an index of important subheadings. \n §BNOTE: This is a dynamic encyclopedia. You will have open access to entries that are relevant to your own state, but entries of people further afield will have to be unlocked. This can be done by a combination of conquering certain regions, unlocking certain technologies, sphering regions, following event chains, etc. If you are civilised and neighbours have studied things, if you have the relevant techs, entries may be activated. Events will inform you if they have updated your encyclopedia. The player will not be informed of passive entry updates through ‘information spread’.

It has been a long time since we dispatched an exploratory mission to the wilds of Bafozh, and the men that set out have long been assumed dead. Now, however, a small merchant vessel sailing the distant Ishnapt ocean has submitted a most extraordinary report to the Admiralty! They stopped by a small island to gather fruits and fresh water, and, alongside the usual locals, they found a community of our own citizens - mutineers from the lower ranks of the transport ship and the expedition - living comfortably on a small island! From what they could gather, our captain is still either imprisoned on this island or living amongst the natives in exile. The Admiralty wonders if we could somehow establish some sort of influence over this land by working out some arrangement with the more amenable mutineers, or the native connections of the exile captain…
And why would we trouble ourselves with such a pitiful island...?

The faiths of the Miiv are multifarious and of all varieties. Beyond the number collected here, there are multitudes more of small ethnic and regional faiths, cults, and sects, but these are the most significant and practiced by the greatest number of the people. Below is an index of our entries. The reader is of course encouraged by the religious authorities to remember that our faith is the TRUE faith and to confine thought about foreign cults to purely speculative and academic boundaries. \n KEY: White: Tehuhrite. Yellow: Vewugist. Red: Kadkohi. Burgundy: Motkohnic. Teal: Wompowushan. Purple: Shamush. Wine: Rechktist. Navy: Momurist. Green: Paorusu. Umber: J'ur. Verdegris: Parqmun. Brown: Juewaeg. Aqua: Gyahki. Orange: Dkåtkang. Pink: Kusii. Black: Pagan.

The editors regrettably inform the reader that the top minds of our country are shamefully ignorant of this topic. They would humbly appeal to the ministers in government to divert more funding to the universities, exploratory expeditions, etc. \n §RNOTE: For whatever reason, your country has not gathered, started with, or acquired information about this topic. You can learn more about the world by conquering, sphering, researching techs, or following event chains.

Kadkohi is a term for the traditional faith of the Gashdzii peoples. Allegedly arising from the miraculous presence of idols and their attendant powerful spirits who protected the embattled tribe of the Gasdhdzii as they fled persecution from the Byotrin in ancient prehistory, it is represented by the major cults of Guzzadt, Buzzamnan, Doshzk, and Maft, and their respective vast networks churches, synods, and congregations carried by the spreading empire. Guzzadt is the patron of toil and discipline, Doshzk of death and authority, Buzzamnan of pleasure and fortune, and Maft of fertility and youth. The major beliefs are the propitiation of these deities as patrons here and in the afterlife, and the belief in a spirit that must be freed from the body after death. The faithful engage in a number of rites, such as honouring gods and their idols and burning bodies. The typical Kadkohi symbol is the quadrine gem with the four heavenly colours.

For the J’ur (meaning, ‘house’),  the existence of a J’ur temple seems to be in some ways prior to any specific belief. Across the Zhadnozho Gid coasts of Bafozh, a vast collection of J’ur temples and meeting houses (ranging from colossal sites in the more populous cities to tiny gardens in areas settled by nonbelievers). can be found. These communal, fraternal, holy, burial, conjugal sites, strictly closed to outsiders, often have social compacts, maritime guilds, charitable organisations and and other social functions attached to them, and each maintain extensive archives of religious texts, omens delivered, and other things. Nonetheless, the J’ur seem to maintain a fairly stable pantheon of powerful gods, heroes, and protectors (most popular are the fused gods, Archs and Chechs, the king who was turned into a gold bar and the lobster that swallowed him), though some temples stray into monotheism or deistic mysticism.
A Fiery $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Zealot of the Synod!

In recent months, a new leader has emerged in the Theocratist movement. A fiery preacher from the provinces has drummed up what seems to be a radical Theocratist league! He openly denounces the government, and calls for the faithful to shun it. He organises massive marches in major cities to demonstrate the might of the Theocratist movement. Moreover, he seems to be gradually converting the major synods of our faith to his movement, which calls for greater clerical involvement in politics. This sinister and charismatic figure is known as well for giving private ministration to aristocratic reactionaries and elites, courting the rich and powerful of the revolutionary conservative movement. The interior ministry sees this figure as certainly a threat to public order, and perhaps a threat even to the integrity of the state.
Do all in our power to subvert this demagogue from behind the scenes!
Have him beheaded and his converts imprisoned!
Let him be, what's the worst he could do?

Motkohnism is a religious movement that grew out of the Kadkohi traditional pantheon in the last two hundred years. The ‘faith of the the stars’ was born when the monk (Dosh) Kauzhut, now called Kauzhut ‘Mifachâzhafta’ (the great diviner), and Kauzhut ‘Donavvat’ ‘the describer’ (among many other honorifics), a small element in the anti-magisterial movement and a nominal member of the church of Guzzadt, had a profound vision of the nature of the world while fleeing south during civil strife. He taught that there was no self after death, and that all would join the dance of the Celestialite (va Motkazh), among many other ethical teachings to be followed once one realized this truth. The Motkohnic faithful do no particular things, but often wear the signs of their teacher, and read and discuss his teachings. There is much emphasis on living rightly in the present, giving the absence of life after death. A typical sign of Motkohnism is the star.

Wompowushan is a term for the vast collection of Poumnian, and larger Diwvish, folk beliefs and religious practices. Its central element is a lack of belief in ‘real death’ upon the cessation of life, and the consequent fanatical preservation and interaction with the bodies of ancestors. Another essential aspect of the taxonomy includes the worship of the emperor, the Pudwou, as a form of world soul. Believers may practice alongside this the veneration of local nature spirits, nobles ancestors, or engage in various rites or Shamushic rituals. The Wompowushan faithful often build vast temples for their ‘sleeping’ ancestors, and the ancestors of the poorer folk are entombed in vast necropoli. The Emperor is seen as a deity, whose divinity extends in a limited way through his servants in the lesser-nobility. The Hatched Sign, or in Poumn, ‘Vudtmruu’ is an ancient Poumnian symbol associated with the boundary of a sacrosanct building.

The Vewugi faith is the term for all those who worship the Great Vewug as their lord and master. The cornerstone of their faith is their common acknowledgement of the miraculous powers and virtues of a truly numinous being (a ‘powerful wizard’) who is allegedly verifiably real and exists in our plane of being. Much of the faith is structured around the observation of his actions and rare speech, and has led to many different schools of interpretation, with many different claims about his actual cosmological and spiritual role. The Vewug is said to live, usually, though he is often invisible or travelling to other realms, in a great Palace in Sesi known as the Drupe. The Vewugist faithful flock to the Drupe, and holymen watch in tireless vigils for his appearance. The typical sign of the Vewug is a face of a man on three interlinked rings, signifying his power, wisdom, and protection.

The Tehuhrite or ‘Sedentarian’ tradition is generally believed to have begun as an ideological prop from neolithic regimes in the vales of northern Ishahfazh, designed to discourage migration and to consequently promote stable tax registrars. The ‘virtues of the solid man’ were first proclaimed by the Philosopher-King Osjunnet of Gohn-Peth, and his various writings on the topic became the germ of a large corpus of Sedentarian philosophy, primarily focused on the virtues of stability, changelessness, and abstract notions of cosmic harmony and splendor. Now, indeed, Sedentarianism has become a complicated legal, spiritual, and philosophical system that dominates much of the north of Ishahfazh. Most typical of the practices of the Sedentarian are the consultation of holy ‘roots men’, satiationary monks who live in the roots of trees or partially buried and are fed by their community, for nearly everything. The Sedenatian symbol is the erect penis-bone, as, according to Tehuhrite teaching, the world began when virile sky impregnated fertile earth.

The Rechktist faith is a popular schism from the Momurist tradition practiced mostly by the northern tribes of Kovazh. Believing, contrary to the Momurists, that the so-called ‘silent god’ is in fact reawakening, and that rebirth and purification is an ongoing process that will be arrived at through the agency of men (as opposed to the Momurist belief in a slow cessation of all spirit and will), the Rechktist Zealots attempt to violently convert others to their pure and austere lifestyle, rather than merely shun the impure and trust the holymen to purify the world, their corpse, etc after their own death (as the Momurists do). Organised into violent warrior-priest clans, Rechktist society is unstable and dynamic, as minor theological disputes often spill over into bloodshed and war. The Rechktist symbol is the awakened face.

The Momurist Faith is an institutional religion practiced by the larger empires of southern Kovazh. The once small regional Humabi idolatry of the millennia old ‘silent god’ has spread, through its institutional maintenance by several Humab and Soxupappi dynasties to be one of the most popular faiths in the world. The world is treated as the dying corpse of a colossal entity whose death coincided with the creation of the universe. The subtle rules of his mind and being, now baked into the fabric of the world, determine right action and purity. The righteous dead, it is believed, will, upon the rebirth of the great silent god, find themselves in the upper echelons of a new order, belonging to the godhead in an essential way. The impure will be cast off as detritus. Momurist diviners spend much time determining right actions through study of the natural world, and giant ‘prayerlands’ are set aside for purity and pure adulation of creation. Passivity, Purity, and Inaction are the virtues most prized by the Momurists. Their symbol is the winged jewel, exemplifying pure rebirth.

The Paorusu ‘witch cults’ of the south west of Kovazh are a large faith believing in a number of persistently reincarnated ‘canonical’ deities. The main practice of worship is the adulation of a number of women, fifteen - in particular, who are considered reincarnated powerful spirits. The faith retains a great degree of scriptures recounting the deeds of these powerful spirits in history and mythic prehistory. The Paorusu clergy maintain a large library of these in Isi, where they also convene synods to confirm the reincarnation of a spirit. Beyond the adulation of the fifteen canon deities, which includes burning offerings brought to their sees, mantras, prayers, and gestures of reverence, the Paorusu faithful also turn to a great many local ‘witch women’ who claim to work magic, like the great deities, as well as believe in universal reincarnation and the transmigration of the soul. The Paorusu symbol is the knotted reed, symbolising eternal recurrence.

The Parqmun are iconoclasts, both with a fanatical need to burn the captured idols and symbols of other faiths, and a ritualistic habit of burning sculpted idols in the signs of the various devils, fallen angels, and cursing spirits of their cosmology. Recognising no other God than the one God ‘Mun’, the Parqmun are the faithful of Mun, shaper of the world and protector of the faithful from their many enemies. Their strict monotheism allows for a great host of devils and sprites, whom they take to be the cause of both many natural disasters, wickedness in men, and to be the tricksters that ensnare the minds of foreign nations and cause them to set up their false gods. The Parqmun scriptures are held in the great temple in Do Dhruzd, presided over by the collection of ‘pure’ child-priests, whose innocence allows them to behold the one sacred image of Mun held therein. Their symbol is the burning idol.

The Gyahki are known as the ‘bauble folk’. Extremely jealous of the various gemstones and jewels that they wear upon their body, usually suspended by chains of precious metal, they believe the soul, through various rituals, and the sanctioning of powerful spirits and gods, can be externalized and preserved, and sometimes conjured into the body of a child. Upon the death of a Gyahkite, a trusted relative will typically bring their soul-jewelry to the great ‘city of souls’, the underground vaults in Rygaas, guarded by their priest-shamans. Their religion is apparently quite an ancient one, with archeologists finding inscribed jewels in the archeological record of the region dated multiple millennia back. The common folk are often not reincarnated unless someone is especially concerned to have them back. They say the soul comes from the ‘cracks of the world’ and ‘the mist of the sea’, and that the quantity of ‘simple’ souls is enormous.

Shamush is a Poumnian etic term for the half-pagan scholarly faith of the Pruunitsh people of the Reuhriz (Wroush or Drangupt in Poumnian) peninsula. It emphasizes the existence of bicephalous snake spirits that pervade the fabric of the world, and has been described as a ‘way of seeing’, rather than a faith. It has developed a large collection of highly esoteric writings about its practice and the relations between its many deities/spirits, and its many apocryphal texts, secretive hereditary schools, and strange doctrines attract mystics and occultists from other nations. In Pruuntish society, the Shamushic teacher typically will live in near darkness for many years, in small houses, attended by students, in an effort to learn better to see the spirits of the world. A common symbol of Shamush is the Two-Headed Snake, The Tower (the sign of Rod, the great teacher), and the Open Mouth.

The Juewaeg faithful are those who worship the evil sprit/powerful deity that allegedly dwells at lake Geshe in the south forests of Bafozh. The faith would be indistinguishable from any other sort of homicidal paganism except for the shocking political authority it wields. The settled priest-kings of Hamog preside over the cult of the spirit of lake Geshe by means of precious objects they grant out to the faithful, the totems of which can be found carried by the many quasi-nomadic peoples of the southern forests, and the bearing of which promises sacrifice and tribute brought to the lake for the great yearly festival where many hundreds of captives are decapitated in the lake. Juewaeg priest kings have told our anthropologists that the totems depicting a headless avian body do not depict the nature of the lake spirit. Nonetheless, this is the only coherent and stable symbol of the cult of the lake God.

Knagtka Kneg, the great prophet, claimed to have been an incarnation of the Sun, and is still worshiped as such in the east coast of Bafozh. It is estimated that he must have lived around 300 years ago, but his faith has spread far and wide. The Dkatkang have no scriptures, but a definitive collection of prayers and odes, spread by word of mouth and kept in memory, means that the heliolatrous traditions of the primitive peoples of this region take on the characteristic of a definite faith, distinguishing them from the miscellaneous animists living among them. Knagtka Kneg is claimed to have been able to multiply foods, raise figures from the dead, and to predict the future. Anthropologists believe that this faith must have developed from a primitive heliolatrous faith, to which Kneg was born into, and which he reformed with his poetry, ethical teachings, and itinerant preaching. Their principle sign is the sun, to which they often append blue prongs, for unclear reasons.

The Kusii Cults of Shobgizob are a collection of practices designed to propitiate the cruel creator god, who they claim to have made the world. They refuse to speak his name, and instead refer to him by euphemism: the cruel one, the grim one, the one-who-sends-large-birds. They are avowed bloodletters, believing the sacrifice of beasts and men can quench his hunger for the lives he himself has created. Their main scriptures, collections of poems and instructions for both sacrifice, and ritual scaring, were, ironically, transcribed in a syllabary created by Vewugist missionaries who hoped to evangelise them. They cite the abysmal state of life, and the plethora of disasters, to describe life as a terrible dream. The principal motif associated with their art is the bloody ring of skulls, reflecting both the cycle of life, and the misery therein, as well as the memento mori and the need for bloodletting.

Since we recently have acquired some J’ur subjects, a number of our anthropologists and hominometricians have endeavoured to make a notable study of the J’ur faith. They have recently delivered a report to the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Academy of Sciences detailing their research methods and their findings. Along with interviewing several J’ur practitioners, they also managed to secure access to the archives of a J’ur temple following its closure and seizure by the state after a failure to pay temple taxes. They have managed to aggregate typical J’ur dieties and practices, such as entrail reading, urn-burial, and have catalogued a number of holy letters and symbols that are always found plastered on J’ur clothing, sails, and textiles. A number of those in the ministry for the colonies and the interior have acquired copies of this report, and the academy has published it in their recent issue of the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ encylopedia.

It is somewhat hard to get one’s hands on the compendious volumes detailing the correct rituals, ablutions, prayers, fasts, motions, and ponderous list of prohibitions kept by the Momurist faithful. Their scribes jealously guard these immense volumes in the massive keeps and towers of the so-called prayerlands. Throughout the centuries small catechism and books of hours to keep have reached the Ishahfazhi libraries, some have been reprinted by our publishers, and indeed some foreign scholars have collected large portions of the rules, but a comprehensive collection has never been assembled. Now, however, since we have established significant influence in Momurist lands, a ‘scholar and adventurer’, one of our overseas secretaries, has contacted the foreign office with a scheme to collaborate with a corrupt monk to smuggle out vast collections of Momurist literature to $CAPITAL$ to be translated and studied. The foreign office sees some use in this for the sake of administration.

The savage Rechktist clans now under our dominion defy comprehension. Fickle, changeable, and violent, they seem ungovernable and inimical to our state, and are always quick to arms. All of our laws seem to offend them, and their people live in self-imposed ghettos in our colonial cities, and are always fractious about taxes. Recently, however, an able regional judge with an interest in foreign cultures has founded a $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Society for the Study of Kovazh. In his first paper to the society, he detailed the intricacies of the Rechktist faith, and the causes of their divergence from Momurist Orthodoxy. He explains, particularly, how those who pay taxes to us are expected let their own blood, or pay for another in the clan to do it, as atonement for their participation in our ‘depraved’ political system. He suggests that taxes be made less frequent, and made into staged ‘requisitions’.

Our recent conquest of Hamog, the barbarous theocracy of the southern forests, has provided the means for an archaeological survey of the Hamogine settlements on the banks of lake Geshe. A number of military surveyors took a number of artifacts back immediately, but a dedicated excavation from the College of Antiquarians of $CAPITAL$ has revealed a number of curious things. It appears that there has been continuous hamogine settlement in this place for nearly six millenia, but despite this they never developed a numerographic or a graphological system, though sacrificial tallies were kept by large piles of knucklebones. The bird-totem has seemingly remained consistent throughout this time.

Poumnia is a term for the land, people, and various incarnations of the ‘Vopudshawrish’, the ‘holy kingdom’, around the Poudwouvas since time immemorial. Dominated by large feudal estates, huge paddy fields organized along the lines of brutal plantation slavery of the Anuvo race of the mountains, a complicated system of military governance by the royal capital, and various subjugated peripheries, Poumnia is a brutal, essentially plantation society, known for its aristocratic outlook, its proud military, and its passive populace. The principal organs of the Poumnain state are the governor-generalships staffed by the aristocratic elite, and the imperial cult and its priests. The apex of the Poumnian state is the Vopudwou, or Pudwou, the God-Emperor who is set to make the sun rise, the ‘golden carp’ and the linchpin of the world. Through his many hundreds of wives, he is said to ‘share’ his divinity with the lesser noble families.

The editors regret to inform the reader that our country sadly is hardly relevant enough to merit its own encylopedia entry. \n §BNOTE: Very sorry, but this country has not been yet given its own encyclopedia entry.

The Miiv is full of a vast and wondrous place full of all sorts of strange states. This subsection of the encyclopedia attempts to categorise the lands of the world by their forms of government and their attendant societies. This part of the encylopedia is sorted into subsections. The editors would like to apologise if any of these entries are out of date due to new political developements.

The recent exploratory expedition we dispatched to Bafozh has been an immense success. In the reaches of the Southern forests, our explorer and his expedition discovered a colossal lake, believed to be the largest in the world by surface area. He and his expedition enjoyed for a week the hospitality of the locals, before eventually heading northeast to the coastline where they met up with a few naval escorts. He reported to the interior ministry not only the uniqueness of the region, but recommended a geological survey be carried out as well, given the tested high amounts of Iron in the water. His local connections are sure to be remembered if we should ever try to establish influence in this region. But here is one more thing. He also reported that he considered the name such a fine lake, and… \n §RNOTE: There is not a lake name for every country.§!
...named it in honur of our country.
... decided that it would be easiest to use the native tongue.

Our recent expedition to Bafozh has yielded startling results. The captain of the expedition steamed into $CAPITAL$ yesterday with news that the linguist of the expedition, a wealthy intellectual, while sailing by a coastal region in which he had proficiency with the language, negotiated, as a private citizen, a number of treaties with the local chieftains and kings, declaring them protectorate to our nation under his own rule, as well as purchasing tracts of their land! He promised them a great amount of his own wealth, and seemingly is angling to be made governor of an overseas protectorate. The captain has admitted a lapse in duty in allowing this to occur, but the colonial office worries that the treaties must be enforced. They estimate, however, that to actually establish effective administration over this region, it would be a sizable expense.
We'd lose face if we didn't take control of this region.
Good heavens, who does he think he is? Absolutley not!

Our recent exploratory expedition to Bafozh, while not yielding many results in terms of ethnography or geography, nonetheless has given the reading public something to cherish. A few months after returning to $CAPITAL$, the captain of the expedition published a memoir of his travels, and his remarkable friendship with his Wushauw guide, who led him across the tractless wilds of Bafozh, and taught him of the strange fauna and flora, his animistic view of the world, and how to survive in the great eastern continent. This remarkably romantic and pan-hoministic tale has captivated and charmed the intelligentsia of the metropole, and softened concerns about the expense or worthiness of colonial ambitions in Bafozh. However, those in the colonies remain hostile and suspicious of their brutish neighbours, and caution ‘the beast-men of Bafozh must be given no quarter!’.

The Paguyti of the plains have always worshiped their lightning God in their holy mountain of Twünazh or Paphüytashu. The great thunderer, they say, makes his will known through striking his holy mountain, which in its own right is the head of a great subterreanan god. The foothills of the mountain are full of populous settlements of their people, and in the hot summer season they bring their fat ruminants into the mountain for grazing, where they harvest the valuable wool. Now, however, we face a dilemma. A number of $COUNTRYCULTURE$ prospectors have, they believe, found massive coal deposits beneath the mountain. A few firms have suggested that the government grant them rights to exploit, but our occupation of the Paguyti lands generally is carried out with a policy of tolerance and latitude. To grant a firm rights to mine in the sacred precincts of the mountain would be to provoke great anger from the Paguyti.

It is well known that wicked foreign races will enslave or enthrall our people without a pause to think. While we do have certain redemptorist societies, what above all leads to the freedom of our racial brethren is their flight from slavery or our conquest of regions that oppress them. Our racial laws grant citizenship to nearly all of those who can prove themselves as belonging to our patrimony. Recently, our government has ferreted out a pocket of our brothers enslaved in our lands. Them and their families are being prepared for liberation and for their citizenship of our nation, and the interior ministry has prepared new documentation for them.
Herein is contained entries related to asorted topics of commerce, botany, and geography.
Herein is contained entries related to political theory, the aims of various political platforms and ideologies, and the various sorts of governments.

Absolutism is the extremist wing of the statist movement. They have come to believe that the state itself is a good, an entity that serves no greater good than itself, and that its members must ultimately be subordinated to it. The state should be seen as an enterprise that succeeds or fails in the preservation and expansion for its own sake of its own power, capacity, and efficiency, and nothing else. The Principle philosophers of absolutist thought are Pazzak III and Bida Gamak.

An absolutist bureaucracy refers to the broadly totalitarian and autocratic bureaucratic systems of government preferred by Absolutist parties. The paradigmatic features are hierarchical parties parasitic on the state, centralist decision-making protocols, secret police networks, nomenklatura-systemic appointments, and the subordination of the citizenry to the growth of state-run enterprises.

Jiishanâg is a large and developed Motkohnic Gashdzii state in southern Ishahfazh. Developed from a confederal arrangement of great landlords, free settlers, and small urban trading cities along the southern coast, with the shattering of the empire it developed a sophisticated parliamentary system and broader state infrastructure to cope with security and self-organization. It was the first state to trade globally and to industrialize, and is known for its tolerance, justice, and developed infrastructure. The origins of the Jiishan state are in the ‘compact of Jaub’, of 699, a mutual defense organisation by the local nobility, who agreed to honour a common Jiisha, or court, which eventually became the judico-parliament of the state. The Jiisha of Jiishanâg holds extensive powers, and most nobles as well as the great towns send representatives, and its vast and august body sits in Nozho for 9 out of 12 months of the year, overseeing most national concerns.

Wapkam is a Poumnian colony on the coast of the Juuruntine territories. Once a chartered company for the extraction of precious metals, rare woods, and beetle-shellac, it gradually attracted a steady trickle of Poumnian freebooters, settlers, traders, etc. seeking freedom from the authoritarian grips of Poumnian governance. While once a mere outpost of the Poumnian state on the strait of Midod and projecting influence into the Zhadnozo, nearly two and a half centuries of colonial settlement has produced a robust state with its own identity and governmental traditions. While still under the nominal suzerainty of the Vopudwou, Wapkam has developed a remarkable tradition of corporate self-governance through the negotiations of the great factors and estate owners, their clients and dependants. The principal organs of the state are the Congress of Estates in Aincha, the President-Director, and the factors of the smaller estates who carry out Wapkami and Estate policy.

More properly the Toshawriz (Poumnian: Doshawrish) of Towourud, the old Towuzhan kingdom has long been a stable presence of southern Ishahfazh. Sometimes tributary of Holy Poumnia, the lords, or king and court, of Towourud have just as often struck their own course, aided by distance, language, and geography. At present the kingdom of Towourud straddles a dangerous line between the dangerous Veyethuns to the north and expensionist Poumnia to the east. Thrakuunt Zaum-Thomon III currently rules, the 7th king of the Zaum-Thomon line, which took power over 146 years ago by ousting the Tributary dynasty of the Zaum-Faemon in a bloody civil war. The kingdom is largely ruled by means of district military governors loyal to the king.

The Poumnian Empire, the holy ‘Vopudshawrish’, ruled by the Vopudwou, the divine emperor, has long projected influence into its periphery and the wider world. This section of the encyclopedia includes a number of states which are nominal tributaries of Poumnia, and Poumnia itself.

There are a great many cultures across the Miiv, from savage beast men of Bafozh, to those of the greatest refinement in Ishahfazh. This section of the encyclopedia surveys the peoples of the world, and their variegated customs.

The Poumnian culture is largely found along the great Poudwouvas river delta and the surrounding lands and hills. Poumnian society is rigid and hierarchical, autocratic, familial, patriarchal, fearful of witches and ancestor-preserving. The Poumnians, as per the rituals and customary beliefs of their land, believe their ancestors continue to ‘live’ in a second form of life after 'death', embalmed and clothed, and communion with the ancestors is a very important aspect of society. Labor in any form is seen as degrading and is only practiced by the lower classes of society. To work hard is not seen as the attributes of a virtuous individual, but that of a slave, and any sign of labor signifies servitude in some form. Poumnians are largely vegetarian. They consume mainly a combination of river grains, fruits, and insects. To consume the flesh of another living creature is looked down on as barbarous and unhygienic.

The Roshupt are a jungle-dwelling folk who speak a Diwvish tongue lying on the border jungles between Poumnia proper and Touworurd. While largely free, they hold no position of prestige in Poumnian society. They are tolerated only because their clan-headsmen profess worship of the emperor. Their strange dialect makes their society relatively insular, but like the Poumnians, they preserve the bodies of the ancestors, though in large jungle cairns, and not the clan home. For many centuries they were mere tributaries of the Pudwou, though in recent years the Poumnian government has set up a number of fortified cities deep in the Roshutan jungle. Unlike the Poumnians, they are hunters as well as farmers, and stalk the largely avian and reptilian fauna of the jungle. The Roshutan also worship a number of forest spirits which are tolerated within the broad notion of Wompouwushan and emperor worship.

Rashuum refers to the people who live in the Poumnian colony of Wapkam. The Rashuum speak a dialect of Poumnian, mixed in with a good degree of naval slang and Aysum borrowings. The basis of the culture is steadfastly Poumnian: autocratic, hierarchical, familial, patriarchal, fearful of witches and ancestor-preserving. More than this, the frontier has consolidated social-solidarity as well as reinforced class lines. More conscious of the virtues of solidarity in the face of many rivals and restive natives, the ‘honour culture’ of aristocratic Poumnia spread down to the lowest warrior-serf of Wapkam. The producing plantation or coastal fortress is as sacrosanct as the clan or lordship, and while social roles are strictly enforced, one feels the factor of a Wapkami plantation has much more affection and paternal care for his laborers than the Poumanian lord.

The Towuzhan people are those of the Toshawriz, or Kingdom, of Towourud. Largely distinguished from the Roshutan people to the east of them by their more sophisticated culture and distinct dialect, Towuzhan society is centered around the large jungle fortresses that house their cities, and beyond these, in the sweltering heat, under the hot and yellow sun, they grow fruit from jungle trees and harvest starchy roots from the sandy soil. Touworud is noted for its relatively placid, tolerant and open attitudes, both unlike the stratified and formal Poumnians or the vigorous, excitable Pruunts of the south. A tradition of birding and poetry are the preserves of the Towuzhan nobility, and the ‘little people’ of the jungle huts maintain a low-culture of popular songs and pastoral languor. The Towuzhan, like the Roshutan, engage less with their dead ancestors than the Poumnians.

The Anuvo are the Byotrin - the giant, glabrous hominids of old Ishahfazh - underclass of Poumnia, long enslaved by the Poumnians (who gave them their name in Poumnian tongue: ‘hill folk’.) Anuvo society and clan structure were effectively destroyed by the Poumnian conquerors, who fought viciously in the slave wars of 500-700 I.R. to defeat and subjugate these tribes and destroy any clan connections or identity among their new slaves. Only a few weak tribes still exist today in the most remote valleys or highest peaks, where Poumnian warriors saw little point or glory in subduing. When an Anuvo dies, instead of their body being cared for, they are cast into the stone foundations of their ruling noble family. This is done to ensure that even in the second stage of life, the Anuvo will continue to serve their master for all eternity. The Anuvo largely speak a rough dialect of Poumnian, with an ancient substrate of the old Anuvan tongue to be found somewhere within.

The Poumnian group of cultures encompasses a number of groups of people who all speak a Diwvish language and are vaguely related to the Poumnian Vopudshawrish (divine kingdom). From the Poumnians themselves, their Anuvo underclass, to the colonial Rashuum, these people share a number of traits, culturally and socially.

Pashdzii, the ancient imperial capital of the Kiidnazh has for centuries been again little but a city state containing the residence of the Emperor, who rules our land in name only. This place bears a storied place in Gashdzii history, the dawning place of Gashdzii identity, the great plateau on which our ancestors took refuge from the Byotrin savages, developed our religious rites, and slowly built an empire. The great temples to all the high gods, the imperial palace complex, the towering workshops, the noble estates, and the immense markets are all still here, and Pashdzii still dominates the east-west trade. Now, however, our state has come to occupy the city. In times past Pashdzii has been occupied by a provincial power, too, but usually homage was paid to the emperor and forces quickly decamped. Our seeming lack of intention to exit has sent ripples of discontent through the old Gashdzii world. To continue to occupy the imperial city would vastly enhance our prestige, but would be breaking the centuries old tradition of honouring the autonomy of the impotent emperor. It would be, in effect, finally ending the pretences of the ancient Imperial dynasty.

Pashdzii, the ancient Imperial capital of our people, the vast metropolis at the heart of the Gashdzii plains, still houses the emperor, who rules all the old Gashdzii lands at least in name. But now, the contumacious soldiers of $FROMCOUNTRY$ have seemingly made a plan to ‘garrison’, for an indefinite amount of time the capital! In what seems to be a sham ceremony, undoubtedly under duress, the emperor has appointed the government of $FROMCOUNTRY$ to be the ‘imperial constable’ and protector of the capital and the lands of the Kiidnazh. Agents from the imperial palace are said to have reached out to the regional powers of the provinces to attempt to make contact with those who might stage an imperial restoration and save the Emperor from his captivity.

Pashdzii is the largest city in Ishahfazh, the ancient imperial capital of the Kiidnazh, the empire of the Gashdzii, which dominated most of southern Ishahfazh for nearly 1000 years, and for many more centuries lay in the hands of her successor states. And Pashdzii is a truly incredible city, with its many millions of residents, its towering workshops, the headquarters of the Kadkohic synods, the imperial palace complex, and its colossal marketplaces, palaces, theaters, libraries - it lies at the forefront of all culture, science, and trade. And now this jewel of Ishahfazhi civilisation has fallen into our hands, though we are not Gashdzii. It appears that the Imperial dynasty had fled - it is not clear where to. The palace complex was locked and our soldiers have made it into a temporary home after breaking down the doors, looting many treasures in the process. There is seeming large-scale resistance to our rule, and soldiers are having some difficulty establishing control, but the military governor assures the department of the interior that order will be restored. We must fear, however, a Gashdzii reaction: they are not likely to quietly watch the despoiling of Pashdzii.

Pashdzii, the ancient Imperial capital of our people, the vast metropolis at the heart of the Gashdzii plains, has been occupied, and seemingly annexed, by the foreign power of $FROMCOUNTRY$! It is not clear where the Imperial family has fled to: some are suggesting Vokonazh, others Vâfaut. In any case, imperial agents have put out a desperate flee to drive the despoiling savages from our great city. And despoiling there is: the treasures of our great civilisation, the imperial archives, the treasures of the synods and the very idols of the high gods are said to be being carried off by thuggish soldiers! And this is to say nothing of the suffering experienced by the people of the capital at the hands of foreign occupation: murder, rapine, torture, etc, are said to be common. Popular movements are already being organised across the old Kiidnazh and even the settled regions beyond the old borders for the liberation of the capital.

Given the recent ascension of the Free-Yoker bands to government in our country, we have a difficult decision to make. Many of the free-yoker revolutionaries see themselves as soldier-citizens of the Sublime Veyethu, the state that carried the revolutionary mantle after the shattering of the old Athisard monarchy. There is a large bloc of our new revolutionary committee who propose incorporating the interim revolutionary state into the larger Veyethun state and ‘completing’ the revolution in our lands. However, there are dissenting voices, playing on regionalism and linguistic prejudice amongst the siethevans, who suggest it may be wiser to strike out on our own.

It appears the people of $FROMCOUNTRY$ have overthrown their wicked aristocratic overlords and established a new Liberationist state. Furthermore, given the status of fromer $FROMCOUNTRY$ as a mere rump state formed after our revolution of 1297, after a few weeks of debating, they have formally petitioned for us to annex them and incorporate them into the true revolutionary inheritor of the old Athisard state! We have made contact with their revolutionary committee and are preparing the infrastructure for the general incorporation of their government into ours, by deputizing a number of their leaders as office holders in our state and passing a number of union acts. The Veyethun state grows ever stronger!

Recent revolutionary changes in the government of Poumnia have ushered in a profound change in our constitution. The dramatic overthrow of Vopudwou, the celestial emperor who we have long worshiped as a god has shaken the very foundation of the world. But now it seems we are at a loss for what to do - his majesty, it seems, is not God, but man. His kingdom fell and the rivers continued to run, and the sun continued to rise. The great carps continue to swim in the river, and the crops continue to grow. In certain regions, many of the imperial temples have been converted to messianic cults of a transcendent, unconquered and reborn world-spirit-emperor, and the Imperial clergy have been eager in encouraging this, bundling it with the spirit of reaction and militant conservatism. Some, however, announce the death-knells of superstition and tyranny, and welcome a more enlightened age.

For centuries we people of the Pudwouvas valley have lain under the intolerable yoke of the noble elite of upper and lower poumnia. Most insulting and troublesome of all the iniquities we suffered was the lordly dependence on Anuvo - that race of stupid, towering, pale, hairless giants brought down by our slavers from the mountains - for much of their labour. We short and stout Poumnians have never been able to compete in the slightest with these beasts, who drive labor prices to zero. Now, since the Liberationist government has been established in the lands of the south, the entire country has erupted in anti-lordly violence, with manors sacked and sections of the Anuvo population massacred or captured by an amorphous class of Poumnian serfs and wretched freemen. It seems apparent the government should establish a dedicated policy to deal with the hated Anuvo populations on our lands.

The recent revolution in Poumnia, and the consequent violence against the Anuvo people, has led in a number of districts the government to deport en-masse all registered Anuvo people. Seeing that the lands of the Ghechi Confederacy are the ancient homeland of the Byotrin people, to which the Anuvo belong, they have chosen the old province of Drit outside their borders to deport the Anuvo to. The Anuvon have been told it was going to be an 'Anuvonwrish' or an Anuvan state, but we of course cannot allow that. Nonetheless, we are obliged to deal with this vast ammount of refugees that the Poumnians have saddled us with.

Poumnia, beneath the jurisdiction of the Pudwou, is a large collection of fiefdoms of the noble houses, oftentimes formally 'military districts' that seemlessly blend into a noble patrimony, peppered by a number of districts governed directly by the Pudwou through the imperial clergy. The noble houses, especially the large ones, hold land up and down the great river, and tend to, as is their right, levy internal customs duties at every border. Their many small territories, like 'gapped teeth' along the river, are perennial interruptions of commerce and the barges. Ultimately, this money flows to the treasury, but modern economists argue that it vastly depresses the economy, and it is source of great resentment among the lesser nobility and the people. The courtiers of the privy council in $CAPITAL$ are discussing the matter today. By abolishing the internal customs, we may stand to gain much! §RNOTE: Both of these options are PERMENANT, pending a revolution, which removes gap toothing.

Our recent expedition to Bafozh has yielded results, which while notably disappointing to those in military and political circles, seemed to have thrilled the scientific world. The captain and one of his adjutant scientists have brought home what seems to be a small swine, not even fit to ride upon. The doctor babbled a lot of things to the colonial minister about the search for the ‘elusive Bafozhi swine’, tales of stalking this solitary creature for miles over scrubland, and the ‘astounding’ implications for both the theory of speciation and the theory of a land-connection in geological time between Ishahfazh and Bafozh, and, based on undeniable similarities he says, the relation between our own proud charging swine and wool-swine, and this strange, pygmy beast that has been dragged back to $CAPITAL$.

The Gashdzii are one of the foremost cultures in Ishahfazh. Spreading from a small community in the center of the continent, in the plateaued savannahs, their vast empire and its successor states have dominated the east and center of the continent of Ishahfazh for the past millennium. Their ruthless and brutal expansion across the continent was characterised by relentless activity, urgency, and wanton cruelty, shaping these strong and enterprising peoples. The Gashdzii are known for their bold and daring characters, their charm, and commonsensical and practical minds. They speak three mutually intelligible dialects, North (or Vokonazhi), West (plateau or high), and South (plains). The colonial Jazhakdi speak a jumbled mix, and have a different cultural identity to all three Ishahfazhi regional identities.

The first Gashdzii colony in Bafozh was established in 789 I.R., by the charter of Emperor Boshashovii the first. From this point onward, a number of Gashdzii states, substates, or principalities have maintained stations, fortresses, or even settler colonies in the east to attempt to open up trade with Ishahfazh. Gradually, three main settled areas took shape: the Hohreathy north, boasting of the Kushnâg state and diminutive Dozhnâg, both largely independent for most of their existence (both having charters as nominal parts of the Empire, from the Pashdzii government), attracting economic settlers seeking freedom and opportunity, the Settlements in Charassland, including Poponazh, the abortive imperial project organised by Jiishanâgi castellans, and Bozzanazh, the young filibuster state, and finally the Theanâg area, including the island, which remains a part of the Jiishanâgi state, as well as the nearby continental shores populated by free settlers.

Kushnâg is the destination for all Gashdzii hopefulness, all those desperate or persecuted of the old empire. Declared an imperial province in 918 after the first settlers arrived in 916, it gradually developed and cultivated an identity of sober farmers. Often referred to as the birthplace of Jazhakdi culture, it boasts of a minor national literature. Major events in its colonial history include the first Hrussan war (1063-7), the ratification of the federal charter (1092), and the Dozhnâg war in 1154. The government is principally a federation of free cities and provincial districts. Many resolutions must be unanimous, leading to a high degree of decentralisation, with powers delegated to municipal corporations and provincial sheriffs/grand jury. The nominal head of state is the Imperial Lieutenant, who is still to this day dispatched from Pashdzii, and maintains a shabby townhouse residence in Niiz Kush.

Poponazh is the largest Jazhakdi state by population, though a majority of these are the subjugated Cherassians. Poponazh was organised originally as a Jiishanâgi trading settlement in 953 by a number of wealthy castellans, merchants, and parliamentarians, and a number of impressive governors, such as Modazh Vazzunak (relative of the famous navigator), slowly subjugated the Cherassian and Gokami princes and tribes. The gradual extension of slave protection laws, increased popular participation in the judicial system, based on Motkohnic values, precipitated a break between the Poponazhi elites and the Parliament in Nozho in 1198. A powerful governor, Paudomenes Fiikazh, organised the colonial soldiery into his private army, and proclaimed independence, resisting lackluster Jiishanâgi bombardments of Shau Maug, constructing a dominical state based on his large slave plantations. A number of revolts in the cities, demanding return to a nâgine system, have challenged the Fiikazh dynasty.

Bozzanazh is the youngest of all the colonial states, settled as late as 1241, the state was organised by Bozza Shazavzhk, a Vokonazhi aristocrat, planter, investor, soldier of fortune, and disgraced naval officer. Bozza privately financed a small military expedition to seize the Gokami fortress on the Island of Dhamit, formerly Vohwan, after Gokami pirates, whom had been entangled with, began infringing upon his privateering and smuggling across the Zhibomgid. He converted the fortress into a private residence, refused to surrender the fortress to the crown of Vokonazh, and rapidly began attempting to organise his newfound lands into a productive agricultural plantation. Small campaigns against the coastal Gokami cleared new lands for the production of tuberous roots. At this point, Bozzonazh is recognised by all major powers except for Vokonazh, and the Island of Dhamit is a shockingly modern city in the east. The government is, essentially, the private property of Bozza, now a decrepit old man.

The Jazhakdi are the colonial Gasdhzii. Ja-zhakd, meaning settler-person, was the Gashdzii term for those who dwelled in the large fortified settlements established in the long, slow march of Gasdhzii culture across Ishahfazh and still ongoing displacement of the peoples, beginning with the great savannah and pushing into the east and west. Those dwelling in the new world, with the first Gashdzii factory established in 789, in what is now Nyut in Wapkam on the straits of Midod, adopted such an identity as fortified settlers, and the name gradually transferred itself to Gasdhzii living in Bafozh. Unlike their metropolitan brothers, the Jazhakdi are known for their scorn of aristocracy, their egalitarian values, and fierce piety. The Jazhakdi speak a mix of the dialects, with a number of quite antiquated terms.

It started slowly at first. A few explorers, surveyors, adventurers, who learned our language and talked to our people. Then, soldiers, labourers, and financiers, and then there was a large, foreign owned and controlled railway in our land! This line has shaped the regional economy, first attracting wage-labourers, those with beasts to rent, and stimulated logging and mining. Now, it carries passengers, freight, and other goods to ports and merchant ships. But this track has also been accused of destroying traditional life: villagers were uprooted, their children flock to the cities, learn the language of the overseas factors, the price to use the rail is extortionate, and allows the foreigners to flood our country and strip it of its wealth. A number of militant anti-foreign societies have formed, and some, it is known, are clearly planning to wreck a line of track, with the aid of those in local governance. We could stop this, or tacitly accede.

A number of savage states have granted our great firms, as well as our government, concessions to build passenger and freight rail in their lands, and indeed some primitive states are so poorly administered that we have only needed to maintain a few guard posts in the tractless wastes and dispensed entirely with the trinket ‘purchases’ of land. These railways have hauled freight and labour out of the interior of the foreign lands into the hands of our merchants, captains, and planters. They are, for all intents and purposes, part of our imperial and fiscal network. Recently, however, the impudent beasts in $FROMCOUNTRY$ have attacked and wrecked a station on the $COUNTRY_ADJ$-$FROMCOUNTRY$ Railway Charter’s main line! Natives, wielding rifles and swords, slaughtered a small guard post in the night, and used some horrid creatures of burden to pull up the sleepers, and scatter the ballast, leading to a spectacular derailment! The government and the investors are crying out for order and justice!

The witch cults of the Southern lands of Kovazh, have been, for a long time, in our societies’ collective knowledge. Travellers and traders to the ‘tea coast’ have long had native friends and contacts who venerate one of the particular deities. But myths abound, and there has not yet been a comprehensive study on this faith, its origins, and its cosmology. One of our citizens, a private trader working in the provinces, has, upon making his fortune, returned home to $CAPITAL$ and has written a large, multivolume assessment of the Parosus faith, connecting the venerated witch-women avatars to what he terms a large, ancient pan-kovan pantheon, of which he also suggests the silent god of the Momurists was once a member. He suggests that the witch-cult developed after literate priestesses were able to write in the hieroglyphics of ancient Kova, in the many years after the first Kovan collapse, during which the temples were centres of life and culture.

The modern world has arrived to $PROVINCENAME$, with, regrettably, all its attendant evils in tow. When the first factories went up, their new brick smokestacks proud in the sun, the town began flourishing, attracting migrants from the countryside, commerce to provide for the burgeoning industrial population, and making the fortunes of many capitalists and merchants. Now, however, a swarthy gloom sits over the town and its since-wretched new denizens: billows of black smoke settle upon the dismal giant slums and tenements that have risen to house an ever-growing workforce of the most wretched of society. A large, dissent, urban reform league has formed to protest conditions, and the legislature is debating how to address the unrest.
Would they prefer to live out their days in a cell instead?
The Statist element's thoughts on urban planning are intriguing...
The Liberationist critique of urbanism is quite stirring...

The Statist element in our society, regrettably, often functions as a society within a society. Denouncing traditional government and commerce as typically ineffectual, statist industrial cooperatives, usually with aid from their wealthy financiers and organisers, are notorious for evading customs, taxes, and developing closed, integrated networks. In a certain province, things have gotten particularly out of hand. A large network of producers and consumers have declared a tax-boycott against the provincial authorities, and have begun establishing their own ‘volunteer’ municipal and provincial comptrollers to build and maintain “private infrastructure”. The regional authorities began negotiations when efforts to stop what is effectively smuggling by force faltered. The major cooperatives say they will comply again if both a number of ‘onerous dues’ are abolished, certain commercial and legal codes rationalised, and ‘corruption and sinecurism’ is reduced in local government.
Just wait until their utopian enterprise fails... then we'll prosecute!
Stall, make hollow promises, and enact piecemeal reform.
Send in the army! Kill them all!

A core tenet of the liberationist critique of traditional society is the rejection of lordly prerogatives over land, and the praise of the village system as the ideal way by which society should be organised. Following the news of the sacking of the capital and the establishment of the free-yoker regime, the provinces have erupted in a conflagration of anti-lordly sentiment. Manors have been set alight, pillaged, and the nobles therein tortured and killed. Registers of feudal documents have been found and destroyed, and it seems that a new settlement has emerged in the countryside of peasants and villagers seizing a great degree of acreage from the nobility. However, since the government arrived in the provinces, to enforce the commonisation of the lands, there has been great resistance to this on the behalf of the new landowners: the once-yoked peasantry. There is currently a debate in the legislature about establishing or identifying titles to land ownership between radical liberationists, and those who are content with the status quo.

Our society, since the establishment of an anti-lordly settlement of land ownership, is a society of peasant smallholders. Rural society is not organised along the lines of large estates owned by an aristocrat-cum-capitalist and managed by a factor, but along the lines of moderately sized, sufficient family farms. Unlike neighbouring societies, where enclosed commons and managed estates have enabled the rapid commercialisation and industrialisation at scale of the agricultural sector, driving large sections of the population to look for urban work, to a notable extent, this has stemmed the flight to the city in our state. Peasants have fewer children, with a mind to pass the farm on to their eldest son - industry grows slower, with less demand for urban commodities - countryside life remains less automated, without the capital to purchase machines and work with economies of scale, making agricultural work in general more labour intensive. While some fear this disadvantages us, it also seems to provide a more stable social configuration.

As industrial changes continue to proliferate throughout our society, we once again are reminded that our relatively unique land tenure pattern somewhat insulates against us from some of the major demographic changes affecting other societies, by reducing the possibility of the consolidation of large agricultural estates and firms.

The recent government reforms effective the collectivisation of agriculture has signified the successful, and largely incident free transition from a society of smallholders and small farms to a modern, collectivised economy. The new law is sure to anger a few holdouts, but the gradual reforms have carried most of the population with them in opinion.

Our recent expedition to Bafozh has returned. They report few incidents, beyond the usual hardships and joys of trekking through the rugged landscape of Bafozhi - fires, insects, floods, freezing cold, sweltering heat, sublime vistas, breathtaking landscapes, unspoilt nature. They made a number of comprehensive survey maps of a number of regions of Bafozh, detailing major rivers, salient topography, soil types, and information on native polities and peoples in this region. Commercial and military circles have already taken interest in these surveys, and propose sending out prospectors or factors to lands earmarked as possibly mineral rich or fertile, or to notably wealthy native communities to capture the local trade in luxuries or staples.

A few months ago we observed the progress of a number of $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ explorers making their way through our land - they stopped at villages, talked to trappers, farmers, nomads, and made a comprehensive survey of our land. Locals report that they made a rendezvous with their transports at a tranquil cove on our coast a few months ago. Now, however, we have seen a deluge of people from $FROMCOUNTRY$ in our land. Merchants, prospectors, and even occasional settlers seemingly have made use of the survey maps made by the $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ government based on the exploratory expedition. We are right to say our nation is increasingly falling under the influence of $FROMCOUNTRY$.

It is often said that our nation languishes, mired in vice and sin, having strayed from the righteous teachings of our fathers. Or at least, so says the new religious league that has formed in many cities, towns, and provinces in our land. Headed by a number of iconoclastic preachers, it is largely organised by a religiously minded laity, who have often run into conflict with the established church and their settled ways. They organise charity efforts, mass meetings, and encourage people even to absent clerical events organised by clergymen they do not deem sufficiently zealous. On the other hand, certain factions within the church, led by more extreme members of the lesser clergy, suggest this a symptom of a church that has been made too weak to meet the spiritual needs of the people, its range of action fettered by an overmighty secular state. The nation has erupted into popular debate about what to do about the relationship between the state and the church, but the consensus seems to be that…
... it is time to throw off the spiritual yoke of the wicked Magi and their pawns!
... a benevolent but authoritative Church-State will restore virtue and righteousness!

In $PROVINCENAME$, a collection of local parishioners have been listening, rather than to the proscribed authorities, but rather a particularly charismatic miller among their own ranks. He seems to have set up his own congregation, preaching his own radical and strange cosmology and interpretation of the faith. Local clergy accuse him of ‘introducing multitudinous errors, dangerous falsehoods, fornicating on holy days, collecting personal tithes, corrupting the youth, and drawing souls away from the true faith into superstition and ignorance’. The clergy itself made a few efforts to quash the heresy, but it appears the local congregation is protecting this notorious man, and themselves have come to believe these atrocious lies! In a shocking confrontation, they declared that they have a right to listen to whatever teachings they choose!
Arrest the leaders and occupy the surrounding countryside!
Let the people of $PROVINCENAME$ be, they are harmless

In one of our provinces, we are seemingly having a lot of administrative problems. Our state is, in many ways, still a pre-modern one. The regional government remains, beyond deputies sent from the central government, who have a degree of influence over these matters, remarkably susceptible to obstruction by aristocrats on local juries and boards. These men of leisure and prominence are typically appointed out of habit and convenience, and usually they are fairly quiescent, but in one province, they have taken it upon themselves to organise the administration. They have established a system of patronage for lesser appointments in the province, seem to be coincidentally underreporting taxes and yields, while all the while taxing their serfs and own subjects oppressively, seemingly lining their pockets and driving local industry into a recession. The local governor has appealed to the central government for the military force to break this ‘cabal’ of corrupt landowners.
The law must be properly enforced!

The expedition we sent to Bafozh has returned with a tale of horror! While their expedition began successfully, and they made progress on charting large sections of the continent, in the lands of a particular savage state, they ran afoul of a native prince who seemed to attempt to rob and then slaughter the expedition! After a week of beleaguered retreat away from the prince, his swineriders, and his savage troops, who apparently harassed the expedition day and night, despite persistent attempts by the expedition to drive him away by firepower, they finally made it out of his lands and to the coastal rendezvous with the military ships. However, not without costs: a number of soldiers were wounded in the skirmishing, and the hardships of harassed retreat left them untreated. Multiple soldiers perished, and others have suffered grievous bodily harms and disability. Whatever happened - errors in translation, transgression of holy precincts, nothing seems to justify the suffering of our expedition.

A great synod is gathering in $CAPITAL$, attracting representatives and theologians from all the Motkohnic world, spurred by an exchange between two eminent theologians. The analects of Kauzhut, ‘Mifachazhafta’, ‘Donavvat’, form the central corpus of Motkohnic doctrine, but the various apocryphal accounts of his floruit inform various, divergent ethnico-juridical traditions. The Motkohnic insistence on absence of meaningful ‘life’ after death, leads its followers to place great, sober, significance on their conduct in this life. Traditional Gashdzii piety suggests the souls of wicked will serve to hold up the very world after death, but Kauzhut taught that the Celestialite could hold the world on the tip of its finger. The ‘dapk’ school, or the retributivist school, emerged quickly after Kauzhut's death, who argue that the community, and the state, have a moral responsibility to punish the wicked, even by torture and the prolonging of life, in this life, and that death is undue freedom. The ‘madmhomak’ or ‘individualist’ school emerged somewhat later, arguing that Kauzhut's teachings have made right action the profound existential burden of the individual.
Make sure the state church sends retributivists, at the very least.
We should encourage the individualist faction, naturally.
This is a great honour for our state!

There is a great oecumenical synod in $FROMCOUNTRY$, hosting Motkohnic scholars and delegates from across the Motkohnic world. We maintain the right to select those who will go from our state church, but the decentralised and personal nature of the Motkohnic faith means that a number of delegates from smaller communities, churches, and unaffiliated private individuals also plan to go. A number of unscrupulous ministers in the state religious colleges have proposed a number of underhanded methods to ensure that principally those who are amenable to our governments view on the matter attend the synod. We must choose between the ‘dapk’ school, or the retributivist school, who argue that the community, and the state, have a moral responsibility to punish the wicked, even by torture and the prolonging of life, in this life, and the ‘madmhomak’ or ‘individualist’ school, who argue that Kauzhut's teachings have made right action the profound existential burden of the individual.
Pay for the transportation of the retributivists across our land.
We in $COUNTRY$ will make sure individualists are sent, of course.
Let the state church send what it likes, and encourage all who wish to go.

We have finally learned of the resolutions of the Great Oecumenical Synod held. The issue of punishment was one of the most contentious issues in the early church, and most corporate bodies chose to adhere, per preference, to a certain legal tradition, and the mainline common-law tactfully maintained a plural attitude. This resolution produces the greatest threat in Motkohnic history of schism and fracture: we are already hearing rumblings of certain state churches and bodies refusing to recognise the verdict. As a Motkohnic state, we have certain legal responsibilities to our subjects: corporate-social-civil bodies as a source of lawgiving and teaching are essential to Motkhonic tradition. If we were to reject the ruling, it would likely enrage certain sections of our population, and enrage those who remain in communion, but should our ministers and churchmen prefer it, or see it more expedient, we could quite rightly claim to be maintaining our own legitimate legal custom.
We will accept the resolutions of the synod.
No, these men have strayed from the teachings. We will go our own way.

The White Flux is a disease that is well known to our society. The disease reliably appears in the historical record around 600 years ago, coming from somewhere in Bafozh. The First Great White Flux epidemic is widely believed to have hastened the uncoupling of the Gashdzii Kiidnazh. It is due to its characteristic hemorrhaging of milky white pus from facial orifices, coughing fits, fever, aches, confusion, delirium, and occasionally bouts of seizures, that the disease is called ‘the White Flux’. Victims seem to eventually lose their capacity for breath due to lung-sac damage and the pus-filled swelling of the lung sacs, and die of hypercapnia and anoxia. It seems to have languished in pockets of society for many years, but recently we have noticed a frighteningly virulent strain in one of our provinces. It seems the pathogens linger for much longer, and the disease is rapidly spreading throughout the cities and towns, with many shuttering their windows and doors, or fleeing to the countryside, in terror of this frightening spectre looming over society, while those afflicted stumble around the empty streets spewing pus and gasping for breath.

The day has arrived. The great Oecumenical synod has convened in $CAPITAL$. Hundreds of eminent clerics, writers, and intellectuals have encamped in the great meeting house of the capital, from all around the world. The sober clerics from Kush, dressed in dour, rough cloth - the slight, nervous, urbane writers from Jiisha - the sturdy, jolly Dhukk preachers, from the borderlands - the weathered hermits from the Gizhpt mountains. It has been over 70 years since the last the Synod convened, at the urging of the Jiishanâgi Lord Minister, over the question of the infinity or creation. This synod proceeds less under the oversight of temporal might, but the proceedings are much the same: our leader, nominal head of our state church, deputises a president and a secretary, and the resolutions are considered binding for all those who consider themselves in communion with the mainline Motkohnic legal corpus, which includes a large number of states and sub-state communities.
