The region gets its name both from its sweltering and humid weather, and the regular practice of burning large parts of the local jungle to push back the local Vuyti and to clear land for farming. With the area first settled by west Gashdzii colonists in the 1160s, it is the youngest state in Ishahfazh, like its ‘brother state’ of Gozonazh. Despite its late settlement, it has managed to attract a remarkable number of colonists, who seek out free land to be burnt away from the jungle. It is dominated by a number of small walled cities, where the ‘old families’, the patrician clans of the early settlers, hold sway. The foremost city among them is Vozza, or Vozzaniz, which came to dominate the six other cities after a series of small scale military conflicts in the early 1200s, when some of the weaker cities sided with the Vuyti of Junugh in attempt to wrest trade from Vozza. The patricians of Vozza typically decide state policy.

Our recent mission to $FROMCOUNTRY$, we have learned, has been successful! A couple missionaries, as well as a number of neophyte natives who are on their way to Sesi to spend some years at the Drupe to learn the practice of Vewug watching and become ordained Seers, and then return to their country, have returned to $CAPITAL$ with a missive from the prince of $FROMCOUNTRY$, who thanks us for our guidance in spreading the favour of the Vewug, and has expressed his hopes that our countries will collaborate on many things in the future, all for the glory of our shared faith. Granted, there is much to do in $FROMCOUNTRY$ still - many of the common folk still must be converted, but this is a great triumph for our faith and our government!
The might of the Vewug is undeniable!

The recent mission we aided in $FROMCOUNTRY$, it seems, has fizzled out. The efforts to set up a press were successful, but much of the aristocracy were totally illiterate and struggled with any instruction, while the local pagan priests were a pernicious influence on the local prince, whispering devilish lies in his ears and slating him against our faith and our missionaries. Gradually, it seems, the prince has lost interest in the Vewugist faith and returned to the barbarous superstitions of his ancestors. The missionaries have become increasingly nervous in what is an increasingly hostile environment, and many of them have fled the capital and returned home, especially the nervous scholars and printers we despatched, while a number of fanatics have indicated that they will fearlessly remain, expecting variously a miraculous intervention from the Vewug, or to be murdered and for their soul to join his hosts in higher planes.

We are, regrettably, tributaries of the great Poumnian Vopudshawrish. The Celestial Emperor in Prousorum demands, on irregular years, contributions to the imperial treasury from the Poumnian states, both in kind, in bullion, and in coinage. Sadly, this year, the tribute has fallen upon us. From most productive districts the Vopudwou is demanding a simple tax that roughly equates to 1000¤ Gashdzii dhamaks, but the extra duties of Pruub and Nuzhdap paid in kind means that those districts effectively pay double. This is always a contentious time in $COUNTRY$, as those who are of a Pruuntish particularist bent always complain greatly, and resist the collection, while those who are pro-imperial are particularly officious and overbearing. The the tax collectors, are simply hoping for the collection to end swiftly, the tribute boats to be loaded, and this whole affair to be over, or for the government to refuse or delay collecting the tribute, which we must decide.

The Pruuntish people are our tributaries, and they are expected to yield to us a number of tributes, both in coinage, bullion, and commodities, which arrive at the great docks at the mouth of the delta, in what is commonly known as ‘the tribute ships’. These tributes are nominally invested in the imperial temples, who usually sell them, with profit to the government. We have noticed, however, that recently, tribute from $FROMCOUNTRY$ has been delayed by several months, and despite a few of their ships docking in our harbours, nothing has arrived. Upon making contact with a few agents in their lands, it appears their government has declined to collect the proscribed tributes and was hoping we would not notice, or care! The imperial clergy excise and tribute office is incensed, and is demanding a retributive war against these impudent upstarts.

The Pruuntish people are our tributaries, and they are expected to yield to us a number of tributes, both in coinage, bullion, and commodities, which arrive at the great docks at the mouth of the delta, in what is commonly known as ‘the tribute ships’. Today a large collection of tribute ships have arrived. The heavy merchantmen, laid heavy with a lastage of all sorts of goods and precious metals, as well as Pruuntish coins, and some imperial coins, have arrived. The goods will be sold on the market, and the coins that aren’t our own will be melted down and then reissued by the imperial mint or sent to the treasury. The docks are awash with activity, as longshoremen unload the great tribute ships and imperial overseers from the clergy direct the transportation of the yields to the temples and the mint.

We are regrettably a tributary of a greater power. They regularly dispatch tyrannical envoys and cruel collectors to assess the wealth of our treasury, and demand exacting payments that siphon away much of the wealth of our land. The time has come again for us to pay our tribute.

We have certain foreign peoples that owe us regular tribute, due to the diplomatic pacts and governmental bonds we have with them. The tributary exchequer court is an autonomous part of the customs board, and makes regular deposits into the state treasury, after calculating and requesting receipts for the costs of transport and the collection of tribute. Today is a day that the court has furnished our government with a great degree of tribute wealth, which the men at the treasury committee gleefully rejoicing of, while the military high command and the public works divisions eagerly eye this bumper crop of funds.

The Island monarchy of the Takemog is an aristocratic kingdom of seafaring Surgoian Tehuhrite people, and some Tufume Vewugist relicts. The unified monarchy of Takemog is a union of various island duchies and kingdoms. Following the invasions of the Sithevan Vewugists in the 400s, the local sedentarian kingdoms in the Moutmaswau, the big island, remained fractured and weak, and the Vewugist conquerors maintained a brutal kingdom that drove most local sedentarians away from the southern islands, and the south coast of Moutmaswau. By the 700s, however, the Petty Kingdom of Souswam had proclaimed a kingdom of the Takemojouy people, having nearly unified Moumasawau, and in the next 300 years, the smaller island kingdoms would, though intermarriage, become parts of the kingdom, and in 1021, the last Tufume kingdom was conquered. The Parlements of the duchies and petty kingdoms still retain a great degree of power, and the government of the kingdom is largely in the hands of local gentry.

The presence of $FROMCOUNTRY$ soldiers in our capital for an extended period of time has long been worrying our government, but finally they have made their purpose clear. From amongst their ranks appeared a small and infuriatingly smug envoy, who announced to us that the tribute contract we have with them is to be altered according to the whims of his government. We have little choice but to suffer and bear whatever they dictate, and no doubt this preemptive show of force is to remind us what can happen if we were to cause trouble when, during the next tribute season, we found out things had changed. The soldiers, the envoy informs us, will be departing soon, and we needn’t worry, he was merely here to inform us of the change.

We have recently informed $FROMCOUNTRY$ that we will be reviewing and altering their tribute contract, and they have, our envoy to $FROMCOUNTRY$ reports, broadly acquiesced to this change. The question remains how we wish to collect the tribute from them.

We are regrettably a tributary of a greater power. They regularly dispatch tyrannical envoys and cruel collectors to assess the wealth of our treasury, and demand exacting payments that siphon away much of the wealth of our land. The time has come again for us to pay our tribute.

The Vupuyti are the semi-arborial arboraloids of the southern jungles of the Maabizhpti peninsula. They are known for their ferocious war masks, and their strange religious rites. In Vuyti culture the elder is venerated. To reach old age is incredibly prestigious, and the words of the clan elders ought to be heeded lest the spirits punish you. The Byuwish is a common ritual observed by Vupuyti elders or ‘Dübs’. It consists of all participating members circling around a large fire, as close as they can bear to sit, and knee to knee. Either servants or slaves then throw locks of the hallucinogenic Nuzhdap repeatedly into the fire throughout the ritual. The participants then share in breathing in the fire's smoke, while masturbating in unison. This ritual is intended to be a dialogue between the spirits and the elders. The Vupuyti largely subsist off of fish and small animals caught in the jungle, as well as some primitive jungle agriculture.

The Paguyti are the docile ruminoids of the plains of south eastern Ishahfazh. They largely organise themselves in large extended families, with one ‘bull’ male and his offspring forming an extended political and military unit. In the present day, most Paguyti families are the charges of an Üytophat shepherd, who fills this role for many, many households. He leads them in battle and directs the building of their settlements. Oftentimes he will raise a successor, who has been captured from a Gashdzii village, or from the Gashdzii slave class in the Paguyti villages, chosen by the collection of bull males who he is responsible for - the Üytophat children themselves are rarely chosen, and often fill special roles in the mountain city. The Paguyti worship Paphüytashu the mountain god of Twünazh, and largely subsist on a diet of fruits and grains. They are typically quite kind, perhaps given their biologically necessary vegetarianism, and generally dislike violence.

The Üytophat are the famous ‘custodian’ class of Paguyti society. The docile Paguyti grazers struggled to cope with the onslaught of Gashdzii settlement, and their vicious exploitation at the hands of the Gashd. They wept that ‘devils’ had been unleashed upon them. At some point, however, Paguyti warchiefs who resisted Gashd settlements by burning frontier villages came to keep the Gashdzii children, and raise them in the ways of the Paguyti. Gradually, the intelligent, captured offspring came to constitute an elite caste of Paguyti society. Guarding their ‘flock’ of Paguyti, these half-wild Sapinoids loath greatly their Gashdzii cousins, and while their privileged position in Paguyti society often gives way to graft and corruption, they remain fiercely devoted to the protection and preservation of a Paguyti way of life from encroachments by slavers and settlers. Like their Paguyti charges, they worship Paphüytashu the mountain god, and largely subsist on a diet of fruits and grains.

Tuoshivaw fell in 951. Then it was a sprawling, thronging, plains city, with many bazaars, inhabitants, and the great palace of the swinelords. The great Budobam Bekob of the Dehuog summoned all the Vewugist nomads of the Fuokuge, the Dibab, and the Ishahgizob to answer to his commands, and his hosts were numerous. The Rannutan dogs came and veritably destroyed the whole thing, burning and slaughtering indiscriminately, and built a small fortress city in its place, settling what Dehuog that remained in meager wooden houses. Now, however, we have come to rule these lands again. Our swineriders have set up a small encampment here again, to watch over the little fortress city, and the dusty tents stirs the mind to thoughts of the city that once stood here. The royal chamberlain suggests, in fact, now that we have driven the slovenly and weak Rannu dogs from our lands once again, that the mighty Bekob of Budobaman take up residence again in Tuoshivaw, and hold court on the mainland!
May the swine kings ride the plains of Fuokuge once again!
And leave the safety of our island? Are you mad?

Deep in the mountains of Rygaas, the strange, giant people have a city. Not one of their miserable piles of hovels, but a great, stone city hewn deep into rock. But curiously, no one lives in it. In many tiny little crevices, one can find deposited jewels, with a small note, usually, written in their winding script. The only living creatures one finds are skittering insects, and ancient priests with brooms who stalk the halls. It is the ‘holy city’ of the Gyahki, where they keep the souls of the dead, they explain. We, regrettably, however, have learned about this after a cadre of our local officers conducting a military survey ransacked heaps of jewels and assaulted priests. It appears they are actually trying to sell the government the precious metals they stole, to convert to currency, of which we could take a cut, but the colonial office warns of repercussions: the rage of the Gyahki faithful as we melt the souls of their ancestors.

Our country is one that has certain regions that engage in the rearing and culling of thralls, or those hominids used for man-flesh cultivation. In most cases, thralls are usually made of one of the more vegetarian hominids, and encouraged to graze in the scrublands, forests, or other hinterlands where they can live ‘as in nature’ and collect foods. As they age, once the thralls have sufficiently reproduced, the men are usually castrated and the women spayed. The absence of sex-hormones encourages them to get flabby, creating a chewy, fatty meat that is prized in the trade. They are then culled at about 15-16 years of age. In the scrublands and hinterlands, it is usually a great festival, with a farmer bringing his troupe of thralls into the stockyards and a great bloodletting is done, with many killed in rapid sequence. Frequently blood puddings are quickly made, and some eyes are consumed raw, while others are pickled for urban markets, and later seasons.

It is hard to believe a people can live in the wild reaches of Gofakidzia at all, but in any case, the Mjhm’an are there. They are oriental insuloids, like many of the people living scattered throughout the Ishnapt Ocean, but their language is so strange and foreign, they must have arrived there a very long time ago. Furthermore, there is only one major current which carries water toward Gofakidzia, which makes it all the more remarkable. To weather the colossal storms that wrack the land, and the cold weather, they build small huts and cottages with thatched grass roofs on the lee sides of mountains and hills, and are seminomadic, cultivating small gardens and fields in the summer, while trapping and hunting in the winters. They believe in an animistic faith that endows all things with spiritual powers, and the spirits themselves are said to come from ‘the spirit world’ to enjoy the world of the living. They are usually clad in furs from the small animals of Gofakidzia.

In Paukzhodo and its environs, it is freezing cold, and there is little reason for our settlers to go to these areas. Our colonial administrators, as well as factors of monopoly fur and lumber companies, collect a lumber or fur tribute from the local Ogrehi communities, and return to warmer climes after they have visited the various stations and tribal communities known to be living there. However, we have noticed a problem emerging with the private fur traders who arrive in Paukzhodo seasonally to hunt the large game. They seem to have turned to grave robbing, coercion, and even murder to collect the pelts of our nominal Ogrehi subjects! The Ogrehi are a hominid uniquely suited to this cold climate, and their anthropic morphology means little tailoring is needed to make a winter suit. Incidentally, we have accumulated a lot of observations about Ogrehi burials, which is of interest to our scholars, but the situation risks setting the Ogrehi against us and spurring resistance to the tribute.

It has often been remarked by our scholars the curious fact that the Kusii cults are entirely restricted to the portion of Shobgizob that hosted settled native Tuqqikian societies before the arrival of colonial administrations. It has been assumed for many years that a settled society allowed for the development of a more sophisticated faith, temples, a priesthood, etc. Now, however, one of our professors, who has studied the gathering ‘bush’ Tuqqikian, and determined they have an extensive shaman class who holds a similar role as the Kusii priests. He has come to the conclusion that in fact the development of a sacrificial faith and strict monotheism facilitate the transition to agriculture and civilisation! It is argued that the demands for temples to carry out these rites encouraged sedentary congregations, and that the need to capture sacrifices encouraged more developed political and military structures.

Our sailors and molluscers go on regular seasonal hunts in our stations in islands out in the great Ishnapt oceans. The great oil-molluscs in these regions grow huge off of grazing on the vast swarms of plankton in these nutritious waters. The oil molluscs caught here are an important part of our oil industry, which is used for producing ammunition, candles, and sealants. But also, it seems, the hunt of the oil mollusc is an important part of the local Zagkhan’s lives. Upon docking in $CAPITAL$, one of our captains has submitted a report to the admiralty detailing his journey, which describes a remarkable hunt by Zagkhans, who went out to sea in several small rafts with only small fibrous sails. Despite this, they managed to take down a very large oil mollusc, and tow it to shore. They explained, through an interpreter, that they use its mantle for tools, and its muscles for food. In fact, they don’t use its fatty and unctuous blubber for anything, which they yielded to the captain!

The ‘Thousand Realms’ is the term for the now shattered Gashdzii empire. Rising in the second century under the sturdy rule of Godhiinimiz I ‘the First and the Great’ (r. 102-149), it spread from the plateau cities of Pashdzii around the Vodmhu river to form a vast continental empire that brought Gasdhzii culture and military might across the great plains of Ishahfazh. It began to experience great difficulties in the late ninth century, the so-called ‘age of undoing’ and experienced a slow and untidy fragmentation and collapse, despite the persistent de jure claims of the emperor in the imperial city, and despite the absence of its soldiers, the old documents, forms of imperial governance, and even economic unity, still hold much important in the Gashdzii world. However, some of the southern states have drifted away from the old slaveholding and agrarian centers of power, and have become more dependent on trade and industry. The ‘imperial reckoning’ is the standard calendar system across the world, formulated first by Godhiinimiz I.

Vokonazh is a collection of hereditary feudal domains on the eastern shores of Ishahfash ruled by the powerful Gashdzii aristocratic family Midodazh. Most properly the term only refers to those states south of the Zhakgizob, the old ‘imperial borderlands’. One of the most centralised and authoritarian states, it broadly weathered the collapse of the Gashdzii empire and has taken much of the mantle as the foremost aristocratic and conservative power in the region. As of 1308, it is ruled by the dynamic prince Gozomedes Midodazh, a bellicose and ambitious young ruler. The government is carried out by a number of ‘constables’ who are sent out from the royal court in Modhag, who oversee the local government in the various provinces, and make sure that the local Dhovs [lords] (who are responsible for the serfs) do not stray from the government line. Hence, the ‘constabulary’, a personal household department of the Midodazh court, is one of the most powerful implements of government.

Pashdzii is the largest city in Ishahfazh and the ancient capital of the Gashdzii empire. It is situated on a large plateau at the headwaters of the Vodhmu river in the vast central plains of Ishahfazh. Now virtually a small independent state, it boasts of the imperial palace, most of the holy synods, imposing edifices of the imperial past, and sprawling slums of hungry mouths attracted by its central role in the trade continental trade network and towering workshops. One may find idle aristocrats lounging in quiet and ancient, tall and narrow, shady and cool, courtyards, secreted away from all the bustle, feeding the birds, smoking Pruub in long pipes, and listening to whispers of politics across the empire, or one may find the sweltering workshop towers of the outer slums, with their labour flags and winch cranes, creating clothes, metalwares, black powder, and tools for the entire Vodmhu valley. Despite the presence of the emperor, much of the government of the city itself is in the hands of the various patrician ‘dining clubs’.

The kingdom of Vâfaut is one of the oldest and proudest pieces of the Kiidnazhi patrimony. Won in the early conquests of Godhiimâdho “the lawgiver” (r. 149-181), the second emperor, from the Byotrin princes who swore nominal fealty to the fourth Poumnian dynasty, it was quickly settled by the great noble families and peopled by eager settlers and missionaries. It has maintained a position as a state with a strong army and has fought numerous border wars with the Poumnians, as well as maintains a protective wardship over many of the inner states of the Vodhmu delta. The current ruling dynasty of Vâfaut, the Utkoz house, maintain the nominal title of ‘imperial constable’, and claim to exercise regional rule in the name of the emperor. The government of Vâfaut is broadly dependent on collaboration between the local aristocrats and nobles of the robe and the central government, with local administration done by joint commissions sat on by hereditary officeholders and intendants appointed by the prince.

Sublime Veyethu is a paternalistic council that emerged in the ruins of the state of Athisoroo, the monarchical Siethevan kingdom. Formed following a revolution in 1297, the ‘Sublime Demotic State’ champions religious freedom and agrarian liberties. Their main governing body is a council chamber, who elects a rotating ‘Lord Protector’ to command the army, navy, gendarme, and other military bodies, all in the same of preserving the popular will and the agricultural settlement. Following the revolution of 1297, the monarchical loyalists retreated to the provincial dutchies of old Athis, and continued to wage war against the Veyethun. With the reactionary monarchists aided by the efforts of the Poumnians, who took the opportunity to meddle in the old Athislands, the war ended in a practical stalemate, and the Veyethun state now controls much of the centre of the old Athisard kingdom. They look eagerly to recapturing these lands, while the monarchical duchies hope to restore the Athisoron kingdom, and return house Athis from exile.

Vugioroo is a term for the monarchical princedom that the short-lived revolutionary state of Sublime Veyethu became after the revolution was defeated. With the rightful heirs of Athis refusing to take a shattered crown, a minor prince of a cadet branch has donned the crown of Chyush, and claims to be ruling a (somewhat artificial) kingdom that happens to be conterminous with the armistice borders of Veyethu. The name is taken from the older geographic term for this region, the vug of the central plains.

There are about five or six powers in Kovazh that have been traditionally deemed by the Ishahfazhis as worthy of negotiating with or sufficiently developed in some way. To this day, these states maintain preponderant influence in Kovazh.

The Great Qooxibi empire is a large dynastic monarchy in eastern Kovazh. It emerged sometime in the early 900s, after the collapse of the Tingi Dyasty of the Gimeng Gon. The Southern Humabi lords of Qooxib, in the Qamo-Qooxib dynasty, seized the claim to be the legitimate protectors of the prayerlands of the silent God, and quickly conquered the lands of the Gimeng, making an alliance with the warlike Soxupappi of the steppe. Like the dynasty of Gimeng Gon, the Qooxib officially claim empire over most of the Fazhri Chrur, the northern states, the southern tributary islands, and the Ourrhond. Their state relies on a careful alliance between the Soxupappi lords and the humabi landlords of the Vetchk river watershed. The Soxupappi guard, the imperial elite regiments, are widely considered the real power in the court of Qooxib.

Ourrhond is a large aristocratic commonwealth in central Kovazh. One part of the larger eastern dynasties, now it is mainly in the hands of regional warlords and governors nominally bound together under one king. The banner of the snake indicates the house of the snake, which currently holds preponderant influence in this elective monarchy. It is under much pressure from regional and overseas powers, with a Vokonazhi trading influence on the southern coasts, the Gussanans and Ratbhoki savages to the west causing endless trouble, and raids from Biori tribesmen. The political situation remains delicate, with the various alliances of lords and Starotsas shifting regularly. Despite this, the seasonal gatherings of the nobility in Andhuspkh are the height of kovan culture, with fine soirees and aristocratic pageantry. Unlike the Qooxib and the Fazhri Chrur, despite being Momurist, they are far more secular and tolerate the playing of music for joy, and most old prayerlands have been occupied by nobles.

The Rhuiqourran empire, despite its small territorial extent, is one of the more powerful empires of Kovazh, governing millions of peoples living in a small space. Founded on the wealth of the tea trade with the Ishahfazhi powers, the Vewugist Chobaji cobaloid warlords managed to iron out a compact agriculture state amongst the rechktist and feroxaloid savages. The handsome and temperate ‘tea coast’ boasts their proud and charming cities, were dressed in their customary yellow caps, their overseers and merchants transport the cargo to Ishahfazhi vessels waiting on the large wharves. The Empire itself has a reputation for inconstancy, regularly revoking and reissuing trading permits to extract better deals. They are under significant pressure from the Pusunetone, who, despite being coreligionists, are known to covet the lands of the emperor.
The Pusunetos of the Great Khan

The Pusunetos of the Great Khan is a new regional power in Kovazh. Riding to power on the backs of the wave of Vewugist fervor that came to Kovazh in the 1000s, the long oppressed Bofungoid Coebeju converted to Vewugism and created a dynamic state that managed to finally end their years of bloody oppression by the feroxaloid anthrophagic paorusu tribute takes of Naiosapa. The Dynasty of the Fobos managed to unite the many Coebeju tribes into a powerful collection of warbands, and hence was called their lord and master. What is translated as ‘khan’ in Coebeju roughly means ‘great warchief’. Their quick and recent formation, however, means the power of their state is changeable and prone to radical changes of policy, as well as brutal internecine wars.

The Serene Kingdom of Anyumb is a centralised island monarchy. Divided between the lowland Anbmedh and the upland Ibhuamn, it is also divided between Vewguist converts and Paosrusu old believers. In many parts of Kovazh, this has the potential for bloody conflagration. Especially, as these faiths both make claim to the real presence of powerful spirits in the world, there is bitter hostility between the various camps. For many years, in the 700s, the isle of Anyumb was wracked by these conflicts, but by 783, the uplanders were vanquished in the great battle of Juonyaeh. Unlike previous efforts to bring peace to the island, the judicious king of the Anbmedh chose to create a court of religious disputes for the differences between the clergy, and gradually, a syncretic tolerance emerged between the Vewugists and the Paorusu witch cultists. The irenic and authoritarian policies of the Kingdom have continued for 500 years, fostering a tradition of absolute submission to the clergy, courts, and king.

Reports from harrowed survivors have been trickling in: A settlement on a remote border has been laid waste by an enormous party of savage Vupuyti raiders. Donning their heinous war masks and wielding various clubs and blowguns, they descended from the trees to enact unspeakable cruelty on the innocent residents. Though we do not know where these marauders came from, the public now calls for vengeance against all Vupuyti savages!

Some time ago, we suffered the loss of our historic administrative capital. Now, however, we have recovered the territory supporting it, and several members of our government are suggesting that we move the administrative capital back to this district. There are in such an area many purpose built buildings for hosting bureaucratic and legislative activity that would surely enhance the grandeur of our state, and we would stop having to work from the various extemporary appropriations that we made after the war through which we lost our capital.

The Ghechi Confederacy is the legacy of an alliance of Byotrish slavers living in the dry highlands and the semi-steppe and semi-desert in central Ishahfazh. In the mid first millennium, While the various iterations of the Poumnian empire carried out repeated raids into the mountains, and the Gashdzii Kiidnazh drove those Byotrins who would become the Shagmodt under the yoke, some small clans of upland and desert Byotrish managed to appease the various regional powers joining in the slave trade of the mountain Byotrins and the plains Byotrins themselves, and taxing the various trade routes and faciliating their transport. They developed a notorious reputation as cruel, self-seeking traitors, but in the present age, they are the only Byotrin country that maintains its independence. The patchwork alliance of clans gradually became a regular assembly of clan leaders, who make binding rules for all the Ghechan tribes. No longer wealthy slavers, they live in abject poverty in the uplands, and deserts.

The most remarkable feature of the Mjhm’an, that all visitors to Gofakidzia always notice, is their strange, soft language with a paucity of vowels. It is wondered how their language became so strange, and most have heretofore attributed it to a simpleness in their minds, or their general primitive state. Now, however, a linguist of ours has come up with a remarkable hypothesis. The landscape of Gofakidzia is dotted with rocky scree in large valleys that are continuously pelted with great amounts of rain. Consequently, rockslides, mudslides, and other dangers of alpine life are many. Their high pitched soft tongue, in fact, thinks our linguist, allows them to shout to each other across the vales without triggering rockslides. Likely those who spent more time in the uplands began speaking like this, and gradually the basic features of the language became this, with the memory of the reason or older tongues long lost.

The Byotrish peoples are a racially unique cluster of cultures in southern Ishahfazh. Tall, strong, glabrous, with large and long legs, in the early part of the first millenia and before, they used to range across the great plains, carrying huge spears, and savaging lesser and weaker peoples, and feasting on manflesh. However, with the rise of Poumnia and the Gashdzii empire, their once immense extent of presence was gradually decreased, and they were captured, enslaved, and reduced to the Anuvo and the Shagmodt slave populations, while the Ghechans, living in the hinterland, remained independent but impoverished, and eventually adopted Vewugism. The visage of a Byotrin still inspires great fear in many, despite that they have been for thousands of years enslaved or impoverished, for their gargantuan bodies and smooth faces seem to evoke fears that originate somewhere in the autonomous nervous system.

The Ghech are the old highland and steppe Byotrish, who did not suffer the complete subjugation of their people like the plains or hills Byotrish. As the empires of the smaller men grew, the Ghech became scavengers of their civilisations, endlessly attracted to the glistening jewels, baubles and jewelry, metal trade goods, and fine silks, which they could not make themselves. They sold their racial brothers into slavery, and managed to eke out an independent existence in the hinterland, applying themselves with now the Gashdzii, next the Poumnians. Today their society does not depend on maniuplating the the Byotrish slavetrade in the mountains, foothills and plains, but the archetypical Ghechan man is still a tall warrior with a large spear, dressed in a garish mix of clothes from many cultures, bedecked in shining piercings, braggadocious, with harsh eyes and a propensity for malicious violence. They live in small stone cities or tents out on the steppe, and largely eat meat from their herd animals and fruit from their orchards.

The Shagmodt are those Byotrin who have been enslaved by the Gashdzii, or have largely lived enough time in their empire to have adopted a specific set of customs and language. They speak a garbled dialect of old Byotrish and plateau Gashdzii, and generally are worshipers of the Kadkohi pantheon, though some slave populations have turned to the Motkohnic faith to distinguish their beliefs from their masters. Shagmodt derisively and literally means ‘piss slave’, perhaps because the original byotrin captives were forced by the Gashdzii to do the most demeaning household tasks, such as cleaning the latrines or carrying out the gongs and bed pans. The plantation slavery in the Gashdzii world is generally organised on an estate basis in the private hands of great planters and aristocrats. It is Shagmodt labour in the Vimâzhfâk and Vodhmuimak that produce a great amount of Ishahzhi grain, fruits, and provender.

It is always a great event when an ambassador from the Kovan imperial cultures returns, because quite frequently they publish a memoir of their time in the diplomatic service, and usually about the tortured and baroque web of alliances in the imperial courts of the south. Particularly, the southern habit of ‘male marriage’ of usually of prurient interest to our public, and the subtle blending of romance, politics, and sensuality, in the brisk southern air and fine palaces tend to make them thrilling reading. They also tend to increase popular, as well as academic, awareness of the habits and cultures of these countries.

The Privy Council has convened to finally settle the ‘aristocratic’ question or ‘estates’ question in the Royal Palace in $CAPITAL$. Amongst the royal courtiers and experts, two decided views have emerged. The more imperially minded and urban voices suggest totally suspending the Gâdân Fi Ja, and elevating the decree of the prince to absolute legislative power, allowing him to convene advisory bodies only as he sees fit. The other voices, those of the radical intellectuals and agrarian reformers, suggest that the loyal serf and peasant must be given a voice. He, they say, is the true son of Vokonazh, and he is more loyal to the Prince than the materialistic and self-seeking aristocrats. By settling up a number of village councils, with jurisdiction over local commoners that could consent to promulgate decrees of the prince, the power of the aristocratic estates could be subverted without having to formally abolish the tripartite assemblies, which would be reduced to ceremonial function.

For many centuries, the Vokonazhi economy thrived on the production of spindleweed. The great estates on the Vodhmu river and in the Eshemi lands of Hakduha produced copious amounts of spindleweed, which were processed by locals and then carried south by merchants, who grew wealthy trading the cloth to the primitive manufacturers of the central empire. However, with the increasing rise in trade with the great powers of Kovazh, the infernal Jiishanagi and the Poumnians have captured a massive amount of spindleweed trade which they import to Ishahfazh in quantities and at scales which our estates cannot compete with. This has sunk many of our once prosperous northern provinces into a severe agricultural depression. However, local aristocrats are disinclined to end the trade, noting our many protective tariffs and subsidies. This means the burden greatly falls upon the common people. Certain voices in the royal chamberlain suggest forcibly converting lands to grain production.

With the restoration of the Kiidnazhi state under our banners, we have to settle the delicate question of the role of the old emperor in Pashdzii. Our dynasty, at this point, carries far more prestige than that of the emperor, but the trouble remains of imperial devotion to him across the Gashdzii lands. Furthermore, he is still the nominal head of our state - we carry at present only the title of ‘imperial constable’. Many are suggesting that the continued presence of an emperor will serve only to create a rival base of power, and ultimate drive the empire into yet another state of collapse, and the solution is a policy of absolute dynastic security: the old emperor and his household must be exiled, and the imperial palace occupied by our current prince. However, it was one dynasty that ruled the old Kiidazh. To exile the emperor would be to uproot the lodestone and foundation of the entire Gashdzii political tradition.

With the restoration of the Kiidnazhi state, the question has emerged among the intellectual public: should the emperors in Pashdzii be restored to the head of our state? For our form of government is not one that is particularly tolerant of monarchy, and the reigns of power lie in the hands of officials, not dynasts. However, the unique connection of the Kiidnazh with the lineage of Godhinimiz the first and the great, whose descendants still live in Pashdzii, means that perhaps there would be greater acquiescence to our rule if we were to hand over power to the dynasty, at least among conservative elements. This, we would have to guarantee, would be accompanied by a commitment to federalism and the preservation of local laws to placate those attached to alternative forms of government.

The Great Kiidnazh, after four centuries of ignominious chaos, has been restored, under the most ancient dynasty of Godhinimiz I. The fractious provincial jadhovs have been brought to heel, the Poumnians have been chastised for their predation of outlying territories, and our army stands truly, unmatched and undefeated. From the utter humiliation of being reduced to a mere city state in Pashdzii, with the emperor at the mercy of the burghers and the clubs, now even high officials quite literally quake before the emperor, the man who has remade the very world in less than a century. Emperor Godhnimiz was occasionally venerated as fifth high god in the Kadkohi pantheon, and it seems this practice has resumed with the current emperor. Such utter veneration and power has set off a wave of fanatical emperor devotion across the Gashdzii world, crying for the Poumnians to be punished yet again, the most outlying territories recovered, and even for the colonial states to be brought under direct rule.

The ‘Thousand Realms’ is the term for the now shattered Gashdzii empire. Rising in the second century under the sturdy rule of Godhiinimiz I ‘the First and the Great’ (r. 102-149), it spread form the plateau cities of Pashdzii around the Vodmhu river to form a vast continental empire that brought Gasdhzii culture and military might across the great plains of Ishahfazh. It began to experience great difficulties in the late ninth century, the so-called ‘age of undoing’ and experienced a slow and untidy fragmentation and collapse, despite the persistent de jure claims of the emperor in the imperial city, and despite the absence of its soldiers, the old documents, forms of imperial governance, and even economic unity, still hold much important in the Gashdzii world. Now, however, it stands reunited, and the foremost state in Ishahfazh.

It happened quite slowly, but then it became a deluge. A few loans called in, a few plants closed down, a few less purchases, then, all of a sudden, a total panic - with debts called in, bonds sold at volume, and huge cuts to wages and employment. It appears our country has fallen into a terrible economic slump. Markets have contracted, industrial firms are closing down, and many thousands of working souls have been thrown into poverty and want. Indeed, even the government is having difficulties paying its bureaucrats, soldiers, and the stipends of the clergy. There are many perspectives on what caused this issue, but the cabinet has convened to attempt to resolve it. Certain voices are in favour of debasing the metal in our mints, in order to print copious amounts of money to pay our bureaucracy at least. Other voices caution that this will drive up prices and create unrest, and we’d be better off waiting the crisis out.

The current depression is causing great hardship and tension in $PROVINCE$. With many men out of employment and little to do all day, they seem to have formed what they describe as a ‘patriotic league’, egged on by extreme xenophobes, to harass foreigners who are blamed for competition, lower wages, less jobs and, more broadly, the entire economic crisis. Tensions reached a boiling point today, with a small mob congregating around the houses and homes of a small minority community. There appears to be great potential for violence if the local gendarme does not step in.

The current depression is, despite all the hardship, driving a lively debate among the intelligentsia and pamphleteers about the causes of modern economic misery. The principal sides of the debate are the statists, who say economic crisis is caused by inefficient management that leads to overproduction, and subsequent crashes, and the liberationists, who decry the entire industrial project as consigned to begetting misery, unemployment, and the slavery of the destitute and exploited common man. The statists advocate for the formation of state supervised consumer-producer cartels, and the scientific planning of the economy, while the liberationists advocate for the closing down of factories and the reclamation of new lands to be distributed to the hungry and destitute. It seems, however, in our country at least, that the consensus seems to be…

It appears the ancient might of the Pudwou has fallen. We are receiving reports that beyond the sea, rebel mobs have sacked Prousorum and deposed the very world soul in a traumatic and tumultuous rebellion. Politically, this changes very little for Wapkam. We have long been practically independent, but it certainly will challenge the reflexive faith of our people. What we have noticed, however, is a number of members of the old government have requested asylum in 'His Majesty's Extramarine Viceroyalty of Bafozh' as they continue to refer to us. The government must decide whether it is worth risking the ire of Poumnia to offer asylum for these old nobles.

Gold is a precious commodity, and it is incredibly rare. In fact, the total amount of gold dug up before the fourteenth century would scarcely fill up four large rooms. Nonetheless, it plays an important role in both the international currency market, and the commodity trade in many societies. Thus, it was of great interest to the treasury that it appears credible that a large gold vein has been discovered in $PROVINCE$ by prospectors. There is already a great hubbub in $CAPITAL$, with many declaring that they intend to pack their bags, travel the great distance to $PROVINCE$ and get rich. Doubtless, for many, this is not likely to happen, but the discovery bodes well for our state.

Some years ago, a great vein of gold was found in $PROVINCE$. $PROVINCE$ itself has become a byword for sudden and fantastical wealth, and many fortunes were both made and lost in prospecting and mining in $PROVINCE$. In recent years, however, it seems as if this fabled land of rivers of gold is becoming one of streams, and now droplets. The great gold mines of $PROVINCE$ are running dry. The eager prospectors are now packing up their bags, and mounting their swine to head to the next awaited great bonanza, and those who remain are left to try to scrounge up a little life in the undeveloped wastes.

In our currently politically vulnerable situation, it seems we have been given a premonition for further negative developments. One of our neighbours has recently elected to withdraw its ambassadorial staff, and shutter its consulates. This, it is felt, could mean only one thing: war. We must brace for this challenge!

In recent months our executive agenda has been entirely stymied by the uncooperative legislature of our government, and the ruling party is unable to govern freely, and remake the nation in its image. After many contentious negotiations, it seems constitutionally possible that we could stack the upper house and create enough members such that we could force our own legislative agenda through the executive. However, this would be sure to cause massive political uproar. For while this isn’t strictly unconstitutional, it goes against the spirit of our laws, and all accepted political tradition. Those endorsing opposing ideologies are sure to be enraged, and we are sure to suffer some international humiliation as well for our untamed legislature. This would have to be carefully done, but it will allow us, on the other hand, to pass most reforms the current government feels are desperately needed for the health of the nation.

The 'Kiidnazh', the 'thousand-realms' was ostensibly the greatest and most dynamic state in history until its shattering around three hundred years ago. Encompassing at its height around 50 million subjects, the domain and law of the emperor carried from the northern reaches to the southern jungles. An integrated political entity for nearly a millennium, the empire rose up from humble beginnings on the central plateaus of Ishahfazh, centered eventually around the imperial city and legendary urban settlement of Pashdzii. Its great weight and imperium carried Gashdzii culture, language, commerce, and peoples across the reaches of the south of Ishafazh, in the long term assimilating or replacing most of the native identities. However, centuries of increasingly corrupt, incompetent, or distracted leadership and spiraling devolution of power into local “Jadhov”s [“Greatlords” - Provincial governors and military commanders] led to a slow and painful decoupling of the bonds of empire. Riven by civil wars, puppet emperors, rebellious provinces, imperial pretenders, the “age of undoing” shattered the empire, and it is widely reckoned that Boshâdâzzi IV, so-called “the sorrowful”, (r. 877-930 I.R.) was the last true emperor of the lineage of Godhiinimiz the first and the great, despite the long and continued presence of a nominal imperial personage in Pashdzii. Now, however, things are changing - our state, to the exclusion of others, for the first time in centuries, holds paramount influence across the old imperial lands. Our rivals lay defeated and submissive or totally conquered. Truly, one trembles to think of this historic moment - across these lands, millions upon millions of souls now look to our state for lawgiving, direction, and hegemony. This is the age of the new empire, and it is the day that the Kiidnazh is reforged from the strewn ruins of greed and strife. In a grand ceremony in Pashdzii, where throning hoards from thousands of miles and millions of homes crowded the streets, today the empire was proclaimed reunited and a constitution was ratified to formally incorporate all our disparate lands under one banner and one sovereign identity.

The political traditions of the south Gashdzii have long been different from our northern neighbors. Much of these lands were settled not during the feudal-aristocratic days of early-high empire, but in the later sturdy years when wagons of settlers went south and east to found small communities of free yeomen and cities of merchant traders. The nominal marcher lords were quick to compromise, and adapt to their advantage, these robust free communities. Forming small confederations of barons and free men-at-arms, the baronial elite were able to maintain profitable plantations worked by landless labor, and the urban conglomerates were able to derive some protection from pressing demands of northern taxes. A gradual tendency to enclosure and plantation stimulated migration to the cities, and a gentle equilibrium of political moderatism and commonwealth emerged. This political tradition, identifiable in the “nâg” or commonwealth, lasted through the shattering of the empire, and has been strengthened by a religious-cultural identity shaped by Motkohnism, the ethico-judical fatalistic faith of the south. Now, indeed, the paramount influence of our state in the southern regions, but not the proper political integration of which, has led to a number of cries for equal representation and the formation of a great southern political confederation. Our ministry has drafted a broad constitution and delegates from across these lands have gathered in $CAPITAL$ to ratify the birth of this new state.

The House of Athis is one of the oldest in Sithevan history, tracing its lineage far back into the prehistory of our Sithevan warbands that struggled against the dour Poumnians and the savage Ghech. The formal branch of Athis ascended the throne over six hundred years ago, and governed a kingdom of the Sithevans with the blessing of the Sublime Vewug undisturbed for centuries. Now, however, the heir to his holy legacy languishes in the court of the Vokonazhi, deprived of his birthright. But why is this? Who would overturn a government ordained by the master of the mondrial plane? Driven from his ancestral home, his family butchered, the house of Athis was overthrown in the year 1297 by the fanatical hoards of Free-Yoker madmen who seized the capital and established their preposterous heretical regime of the ‘Sublime Veyethu’! But now we are in a position to right these wrongs… having reunified the lands of the Sitheve under our hegemony, our government has invited the scion of house Athis to return from his ignominious exile, and to retake the mantle of government and don once more the Crown of the Chyush! Hurrah for the Sithevan People! Hurrah for House Athis! Hurrah for the will of the Mighty Vewug!

We peoples of Pruuntia have long languished in the shadow of the Poumnian empire. Our tongue is not far off from the Poumnians of the north, and indeed our kings, temples, and small principalities have long been considered tributary parts of their great celestial empire. But we are a different sort of folk than they. We are seafarers and fishermen, where they are a staid, agricultural people. We are joyous and free, where they are dour slaves of the empire. And for centuries our people have kept our own traditions and folkways around the ‘Shamush’ way, the awareness of the bicephalous serpentine spirits that knit the very world together, despite the presence of the imperial cult among our elites. But in recent years, more and more of our poets, our writers, even local princes themselves speak of Shamush lore, and above all what that means for one who would call themselves a Pruunt. For too long, cries on impassioned writer, we have languished under the cultural, political, and religious tyranny of the government of the Vopudwou. We should have our our faith, our own state, our own destiny, as the Pruuntish people! Proud, noble seafarers! It is we who first journeyed to Kovazh, many centuries ago. It is we who hunt the great bloated molluscs of the Diwvo depths, and trawl the thronging shoals of the western oceans. We are not Poumnians, we are Pruuntish people, and we follow the Shamush way! The government, it is said, should close the imperial temples, stop sending offerings to the capital, and above all, they should call the emperor not a god but a despot, if they wish to be a Pruuntish government. It is time we heard this call. To challenge the Poumnian empire like this would surely lead to a swift and terrible reaction from their large army - the empire has never been challenged in such away in recorded memory, and the cult of the Divine Vopudwou is the very foundation of their statehood.

There has never been in history a unified Pruuntish state. Long fractured amongst rival sea-lords, small ecclesiastical dominions, petty merchant republics, and above all tyrannized by the Poumnians to the north, our lands now lay for the first time in history unified, sovereign, and unbowed. It is we who challenged the Poumnian ‘elder brother’ and locked horns with the imperialist cause. Today, then, we proclaim the Pruuntawrish - the Pruuntish state. In a grand ceremony in $CAPITAL$, attended by the scions of the old naval houses, the merchant families, the Shamush teacher-priest dynasties, and above all the cheering populace, the minister of state proclaimed the formal adoption of this new name and the promulgation of a unified government for Pruunts everywhere. There will be many challenges ahead as we strive to fend for ourselves in the international political arena, but today is truly a momentous, perhaps the most momentous, day in Pruuntish history.

The diminutive region known as 'Dhuknâg' has always had a difficult and tenuous existence. On the borders between the Gashdzii empire and ancient Poumnia, this flexible borderland has developed a flimsy identity around its frontier status and consequent tradition of moderate autonomy. However, now that we are a major regional power, a number of bureaucrats of the foreign office have made the curious suggestion that this region needs to be annexed for security reasons. Long an unsure part of both Poumnia and the Gashdzii empire, they believe we could easily trump up a story of ‘effective administration’ and a ‘supervised district’ despite the strong governance of the region as it is. If done swiftly, this region may be an important asset for our security in continental and regional politics.

Recent changes in the government of Poumnia have forced us to reflect on the religious constitution of our country. The dramatic overthrow of the Vopudwou, their celestial empire who is worshiped as a god, not only in their kingdom but all around the circle sea, into our Pruuntish lands, has shaken the very foundation of the world. We have many temples to the emperor, and most of our elites belong to the imperial cult, sending small offerings across the sea yearly to pray to his majesty. But now it seems we are at a loss for what to do - his majesty, it seems, is not God, but man. His kingdom fell and the rivers continued to run, and the sun continued to rise. In Poumnia many of their temples have been converted to messianic cults of a transcendent, unconquered and reborn world-spirit-emperor, but we in Pruuntia have our own indigenous faith, that of the ‘Shamush’ way. These esoteric folkways have been preserved by itinerant preachers, secretive religious schools, and village rites. Above all Shamush is almost less a faith, but a ‘way of seeing’. It might be prudent to dissociate our government from the dying empire, and publicly endorse Shamush rites for the first time in recorded memory.

We Byotrish have always been foreign to our neighbors. Tall, strong, and fast, we are not like those stout little fellows who came to live in the river and on the plateau and eastern plains. For indeed it was we who lived there long before those plateau men came with their boars from the east. The poets and bards sing of times of yore when we used to range across the vast plains, heroic warriors with sturdy frames, able to fight five of the stout and low men with ease. Now, though, it is not like this. Driven into the mountains, we live a complacent and impoverished life on the margins of civilization, while our racial brothers, our fellow Ghechan people, toil on the fields of the stout men in Poumnia and Gashdziik. How long must this state of affairs persist, lament our authors, our leaders, and indeed all those who have seen the suffering of the slaves of the lowlands? Shall we be blind to our fate? Nay! In recent years not only has our confederation gained material strength, political order, but the spirit of our people have been stirred to a new national consciousness of our racial destiny to right the wrongs of a 1000 years and liberate our brothers! This is the "the Ghan-Gheecha idea" - the unabashed birthright of the Ghechi, whether Byotrin, Anuvo, or Shagmodt!

The Byotrish of the Poudwouvas have toiled for so many centuries in slavery not only do most of them speak a wretched Poumnian patois tongue, but they happily call themselves ‘Anuvo’, the slur for us that the Poumnian brutes speak bitterly. Nonetheless, they are our racial brethren, and we have a historic responsibility to free them from their suffering. For it was the Poumnians above all who were most cruel to our people - it was they who were not content just to drive us from our lands, but continued to stage slave raids into our lands for centuries. To recover even a fraction of these lands would bring unending glory to our forces. It is time to right the sins of history with blood!

The Byotrish of the plains have toiled for so many centuries in slavery not only do most of them speak a wretched Gashdzii patois tongue, but they have become alarmingly attached to the several heathen and idolatrous faiths of the intellectually backwards Gashdzii, doubtless an abomination in the eyes of the Great Vewug. The faster this situation is remedied, the better. We must retake the nearest lands stolen from us long ago, and let our warrior range free over the planes of the east once again!

The west Ghech territories have long lain under the yoke of the Sithevan peoples. Politically driven from these lands long ago, some of our people still scrape by in a meager living along these plains and on the banks of the great lake. While effectively governed by the Sithevans, we surely can make an irredentist claim to these lands. These long fallen territories must be recovered too!

For all of known history the great empty white sands of the Bauxae have remained a wild and dangerous place. To our northern border towns and cities it is known for harboring bandits and Biori raiders who for centuries have made forays into our land to loot homes, pillage temples, and capture children to be made into thralls, but now after a series of centralization and modernization projects our government now finally has the means to do something about this hazardous wasteland. Our generals tell us it would take one swift military operation to occupy the desert, subdue the Biori tribesmen, and finally bring peace to the northlands.

The crown of the Qooxib has long put aside vast lands for relentless contemplation and worship of the silent god. Only through perfect ritual purity can His sublime and exacting will be pleased, and the world be a perfect mirror of this sacrosanct will. The slender prayer towers of these monastic reservations stand tall and imperiously over rolling valleys, in which only are heard the endless reminiscent bells tolling to drown the words and thoughts of men, and these lands are bounded by the little old stones that every Qooxiban knows to cross unpurified means to offend God. For many hundreds of years the state has encouraged the maintenance of these monastic domains within the patrimony of empire, considering it a pious policy to safeguard the worshiplands. Now, however, it is a new age. The first rolling automotives imported from Ishahfazh have thundered through our lands, the mechanical presses churn out constant gazettes and pamphlets, and towers belching soot and ash now rise beside their older kin which housed men - everyone agrees that life has gotten faster, dirtier, and chattier. The prayer lands, say the writers and the modernisers, are thus an anachronism. The tenants toll under the tyranny of zealot monks living in a different century, and the boundary stones block the swift movement of worldly goods. Extreme brutality and all sorts of evils persist - slavery, gougings for impurities, draconian legal dues, and worse. The modern state must do away with these abuses and abolish the prayerlands for the sake of good governance - we must please the silent god, all of us, in our own lives, and not trust distant monks to do it for us.

The 'Great Drupe' is a site of immense importance to the Vewugi faith. It is a sprawling ancient palace with seemingly endless labyrinthine hallways and rooms inhabited by hundreds of Vewugi holy men. Inside, it is reported that residing within this palace is the Great Vewug himself, an immensely powerful spirit or deity which the Vewugis worship. The Vewug is said to appear before certain holy men at certain times within the palace, and the Vewug's every movement or word spoken is to be recorded and later deliberated on and interpreted. Perhaps it comes from collective delusion or the use of the hallucinogenic Nuzhdap - these fanatics are certain that this being exists within these very walls. But now that we have occupied the surrounding landscape, many high-ranking military men have floated the idea of razing this palace once and for all. This will surely be a devastating blow to our enemy and to the entirety of the Vewugist faith, but it will most certainly enrage Vewugists across the world and drive them to violence against us.

The Oujoy people, in ancient times, were one. A large kingdom of Oujoury, the kingdom of Surgoia, ruled most of the northeastern vales from the 100s to the 500s, before suffering colossal collapse with the advent of the Bogorugi and the larger Vewugist migrations. And from such a point onward, the customs and nature of our peoples diverged. The Mamajouy, the ‘tall’ brother, who stood against the Vewugist conquerors, continued to speak a purer Oujouy tongue, to use the courtly rituals of ancient Surgoia, and lived a far more agrarian lifestyle, while the Yamajouy, the ‘shorter’ brother, took gradually to the customs of the Bogorans: their dialect borrowed from the stilted, laconic tongue of the Bogorans, their began to organise their society in terms of clanship and hetmanship, and they took to a martial and pastoral lifestyle far easier. Now, however, with the Borogan conquers defeated, and the Yamajouy much under our sway, it is considered prudent to adopt, in a congress of the Yamajoury clans, the Hetmanship of All the Yamajouy, and to reunify our once fractured national identity!

For centuries, Poumnian sailors and soldiers have stopped along the shores of Deuuyeuru to trade and resupply. Some of these Poumnians married Pruuntish women and settled in the capital city of Aaykeum. Many of these expatriates rose to become some of the most important and affluent citizens of Deuuyeuru and have proved invaluable in asserting Poumnian influence over the island. In recent years, however, with the rise of Pruuntish nationalism and Shamushi snake-worship, tensions in Aaykeum have become shockingly high, with several assassinations of prominent Poumnians. Many of these expatriates fear they will soon be forced to flee the island or face violence at the hands of radicals. However, officials in our government think we could use our influence and military to pressure the Deuuyeuruhn government to accept annexation and military occupation to safeguard our citizens and their assets, while also asserting our dominance across the entire Diwvish Sea

The bushlands have become a place of increasing violent conflict. Outside the borders of $COUNTRY$, Bafozhi beast-men, not tied to the land, are able to roam and pillage freely. Encroaching Gâshdzii settlers do battle with Hohraeth and Hrusaan war parties nearly every day, and stories of heinous Bafozhi-orchestrated massacres have become the norm in our newspapers. Public opinion has become staunchly in favor of military action to bring these wild lands under control, put these Bafozhis to work tilling the fields, and divide the newly acquired estates to eager would-be settlers back in $CAPITAL$.

The Ishagizob to our south has always remained a free and lawless place. No fearsome conquerors or great emperors of old ever bothered to subjugate these vast barren lands, and only in recent years has the idea of conquering this great desert been floated in government. This desert is now seen as a security threat, a wide open and unmonitored patch of land that leads right into the heart of $COUNTRY_ADJ$ territory. To conquer these lands would be simple and would assure us a more secure border, putting our officials and people at ease.

The Zatgizob to our west has always remained a free and lawless place. No fearsome conquerors or great emperors of old ever bothered to subjugate these vast barren lands, and only in recent years has the idea of conquering this great desert been floated in government. This desert is now seen as a security threat, a wide open and unmonitored patch of land that leads right into the heart of $COUNTRY_ADJ$ territory. To conquer these lands would be simple and would assure us a more secure border, putting our officials and people at ease.

Our state is a strange one. The empire is secured by virtue of the immense wealth and private property of the imperial dynasty, and the nominally private treasury of the house Rannu acts effectively as the state treasury. In most other states, the household of the monarchy has been gradually separated from the formal state apparatus, but in our empire, we exist in an uneasy equilibrium of a preponderant imperial household, and a nominal ‘political’ bureaucracy of the old tribute treaties and lordly districts of the Unnahu and Uttobanhu elites, who jealously guard their ancestral privileges. Beyond this, the Empire maintains massive estates in the Ngoghu lands of Vadobeth, conquered many centuries ago, in the 7th century, and still held by the imperial family and their many thousands of overseers, adjutants, and factors. But the Ngoghu speak a language remarkably similar to us, and centuries ago before the conquest, the Vadobethi lands were a mere geographic distinction between the three ‘brothers of the north’, the Duttuphti peoples. Embattled by enemies on all sides, we can no longer allow our archaic political system to sow discord between the Ngoghu and the traditional elites. We must radically reform the imperial parliament, to include equal representation in all districts of the country, to include a collection of ennobled Ngoghu landowners in the imperial upper house, and finally we must relinquish a great degree of private land to be free Ngoghu districts. In turn, it is hoped, the Ngoghu people will mobilize their people for conflict in times of crisis and assist the $COUNTRY$ in with higher taxes and further material production.

Our state laws are explicit on the illegality of any sort of arrangements of serfdom or land-bondage. The strict enforcement of these is the business of our censors, tax collectors and assessors, and regional government officials, who work to extend this legislation into all the reaches of our great territory in order to abolish this archaic practice wherever it may be.

Our state laws explicitly forbid the rearing, culling, vending, driving, transhumance, pasturing, breeding, and above all consuming the flesh of hominid cattle, or ‘thralls’. Commonly the preserve of ranchers and herdsmen in the desolate reaches or barbarous uplands of our society, the abolition and enforcement of this policy is usually the purview of regional sheriffs and the mounted gendarme, who work tirelessly to eradicate the practice wherever they may find it.

Thralldom - the practice of keeping other species of hominid as laboring livestock - is a very common practice in the more desolate and barren parts of the world. In marginal economies of small freeholding peasants, especially in hinterland regions like mountain uplands, arid scrub, and rocky wastes, where even the most hardy ruminants and other grazing animals struggle to survive, keeping slaves whom you plan to eat is sometimes a common practice, despite the long cycle of raising them. However, this practice in recent years has not only been condemned as barbaric, given recent cultural exchange with the civilized others across the oceans, but also seems manifestly backwards and inefficient. Government economists project that by compelling our subjects to legally treat their thralls as slaves, not only will marginal land be freed for mining, prospect, or more efficient agricultural usage, but the labor redirection will be highly beneficial - once idle thralls lolling about in the scraglands eating small lizards and other meager foods will likely be sold to our great corporations, departments, and slave merchants, redirecting the labor of potentially hundreds of thousands to profitable enterprises. However, there is likely to be a great backlash. Thrall keeping is deeply ingrained in the cultural patterns of homesteaders and common men, who prize it as ‘the finest meat’ and the culling of thralls is in some places even celebrated under the sanction of the local religious authorities. Even some traditional men in the cities or the great estates prize it and consume it for cultural reasons, believing that the proteins of manflesh are curative to the brain and eyes, and was what allowed our civilization to rise and prosper. Indeed, none can doubt that it is highly nutritious - very likely because these other hominids are so close to us biologically, they carry all that we need to survive…

To belong to the imperial citizenship, in these lands, has been seen as a great privilege and honor - to serve in the divine plan of the world spirit, the holy Vopudwou (Emperor) who makes the sun rise and the rivers run is a near sacrosanct responsibility. Typically, it has belonged to the governing aristocracy, the servants of the empire, and the soldiery (among other honored figures here and abroad). However, the extension of citizenship in the Pruuntish states to the south, since time immemorial our nominal tributaries, has always been curious. A disdain for their garbled dialect, strange morals, and raucous natures has inclined our people to keep a distance from their government and practices - the citizenship is granted sparsely and delicately in these lands, and they have largely been left govern themselves provided the nominal tributes arrive and due respect is accorded. Now, however, since our direct annexation of a variety of loyal Pruuntish states, our interior ministry has come up with a curious proposal. A broad and sweeping extension of the imperial citizenship through the political and social elites and the military of Pruuntia, as well as bilingual bureaucratic documentation in the southern peninsula, would allow for closer integration and easier governance of the Pruuntish territories. It would pave the way, the ministry argues, for a broad expansion of our tax base, and increase social and political stability within these regions, righting, really, a sense of injustice to these sturdy men of the south, and extending the imperial honors to our seafaring peninsular brothers. Extension of such a citizenship, however, would preclude the preservation of tributary status for most of these principalities, and we would be effectively abolishing the tributary system in the south - the interior ministry expects some resistance should some of these petty states try to preserve their haphazard existence against our effective occupation.

Paknâg is a land that has long been plagued by a tradition of social banditry. Since the disentanglement of the empire and the attendant periods of violence as borders were readjusted, Paknâg’s central position has left it a regular victim to the transit of pillaging armies. The perennial devestion, and the cruelty of the castellan lords who barely kept order in the region usually, allowed for the development of a tradition of social bandits living on the margins of society. These freebooters and warriors in previous times often lent their weapons to the defense of farming communities or worked as mercenaries abroad, but now, as the confederal Paknâg state is better able to keep order, they have merely become a menace to the east-west trade out of the south. Now, however, as the coercive infrastructure of our state has greatly grown, the interior ministry feels we are in possession of the power to wage a campaign for the permanent suppression of banditry in Paknâg. By destroying the bandits and implementing extensive surveillance efforts, as well as conscripting unruly youth, the ministry feels we can finally put a rest to this cyclical violence.

The northern principalities or Realm is a term for a number of diminutive princely states that cling to the edge of central Gashdziik where the Vodmhu river reaches the northern deserts. Their dialect and martial culture make them much more similar to the people of Vokonazh, the ‘northern Gashdzii’, rather than those closer to the Gashdzii heartland. Sometimes under the dominion of the lords of the East, they nevertheless cling to independence and often associate with the west. In recent months, our government has deemed it essential to bring these regions under our formal legal control - the prospect of them falling decidedly under the influence of the western lords is too much of a security threat. We have a number of historic de jure claims to these lands based on Viceroyal jurisdictions granted by various emperors, which the government has invoked to attempt to legitimise our claims to these regions.

The Chiibnazh, the ‘defensive state’, ‘citadel league’, of the times of trouble - the first anti-magesterialist instability that began over 150 years ago, was a military union with political functions that flourished for around 10 years in the lands of central Gashdziik. For central Gashdziik for centuries has been a fractured and vulnerable realm. The titular emperor rules in great Pashdzii, but the Jadhovs (greatlords) of the provinces rule with iron fists as lords of separate states. Worst still, we are prey to the ambitions of the lords on our borders. The great southern states treat us with little but contempt, Vokozazh has long pretended to the imperial mantle and had regularly occupied the inland in various wars, and for many ages has lonely and proud Vafaut stood, beleaguered, against the might of Poumnia, who would dismantle our fortresses and make us tributaries. In recent years, there is talk of reviving the Chiibnazh, this time with even greater centralised political authority. These dreams have often failed - in the lands of the old empire, political fragmentation, bitter enmity between the local lordship, and the political designs of the border powers, who invoke imperial levy laws, feudal rites, and sly manipulation to rule our states, leave our people fraught with suspicious and ill-inclined to work together. Not anymore, however! Our paramount influence in central Gashdziik has brought us to a position where we can organise the Chiibnazh once more - indeed, as we speak delegates are assembling in $CAPITAL$ to swear loyalty to the new flag. Gone are the days when the little states of the Empire will be weak to the predatory borderlands and southern marcher lords!
End the Right to the Familiar

The Right to the Familiar is a traditional Tehuhrite legal tradition that allows those whose way of life has been disrupted by others, politicians or government officials to appeal to the autonomous legal-religious scholarly community for a verdict on the right to maintain traditional ways of life. Pending the holy man or scholar’s condemnation of the disruptions, there is usually great pressure to right these wrongs. Historically, this was often invoked in conflicts between agricultural communities and herdsmen, but recently it has been applied increasingly to disruptions attendant in canal building and factory construction. However, with the recent changes in our government, and the advent of a statist administration, we may finally dispose of this obstacle to progress, and allow the forces of modernity to range across our land. By refusing to acknowledge verdicts by the holy men, arresting those that issue verdicts, and making our state officially secular, we will make it clear that this old right will no longer be respected. No longer will religious intransigence and backward zealotry impede the material progress of civilization!

There has been, sadly, a recent flare up on banditry in Paknâg! Social brigands are wreaking havoc across these lands and disrupting life greatly. We must organise and equip a section of the gendarmerie to go and destroy these devilish troublemakers. This will be expensive, and require persistent efforts, not the casual work of soldiers, to track, find, and destroy bandits that range out on the great plains, who hide in glades in the wooded areas, as well as arrest their supporters in the towns and villages.

The wild stormy reaches of Paukzhodo, ‘The Land of the Spears’ (named so either because of its hostile inhabitants or the large horned animals that graze in its cool forests). Lying just of the northern coast of Ishahfazh, its own northern coast hugs the great northern sea and is buffeted by brutal storms and cold winds, but it's more temperate south is marked by large river complexes populated by fishing, hunting, and farming communities who bring strange pelts and fine timber out of the north. These hardy folk, both the troglodyte Ogrehi of the north and semi-subterranean Nahu of the southern coasts have tended to live in low, underhill, semi-buried settlements For this land is dangerously foreboding: wracked by great storms and host to dangerous extremophile bacteria, our settlers, not suited to this peculiar lifestyle, have mostly avoided this place. Now, however, our state has established a number of settlements, actually, in the ungoverned reaches of this land. The foreign ministry is increasingly thus interested in the lands of Hûpênnohu, the state of the Purgure. The Purgure are known as bold warriors, drinkers, and adventurers, tinged with the paganism of Paukzhodo, who speak a language similar to that of the Rannutan Elite, but seemingly have settled the southern coasts here several centuries ago, as slavers, traders, and piratical warriors. These fertile lands, however, are clumsily managed, and we have already wrung several concessions from them, to own roads and manage ports to facilitate our settlement. The foreign ministry suggests we urgently should establish protectorate over these lands, to protect our further settlements, lest some other power could seize these lands and menace our colonies.
